Constantino II concentra su monarquía en: Constantine II concentrates his monarchy on Kartli.
Continuidad de la herencia borgoñona en: Continuity of the Burgundian heritage in the southern Netherlands.
Continuidad de la herencia borgoñona; di: Continuity of the Burgundian heritage; different from the French Duchy of Burgundy.
Continuidad del gobierno delegado bajo M: Continuity of the delegated government under Maria Teresa until her death in 1741.
Continuó la casa condal fundada por Robe: The county house founded by Robert I continued. His family combined Dreux's estate with marriages that opened new political possibilities for his children.
Continuó la rama de Castellbó y fue padr: He continued the branch of Castellbó and was the father of Matthew and Elizabeth. Neither of the two inherited Foix from Gastón Fébus by direct descent: the link came from a collateral line. His incorporation into the tree allows us to follow that relationship without making the successor son of the previous ruler.
Continuó la rama de Mukhrani fundada por: He continued the branch of Mukhrani founded by his father Bagrat. His offspring provide the link between the first princes of this domain and the kings of Kartli of the seventeenth century.
Continúa como principado eclesiástico de: It continues as an ecclesiastical principality after Westphalia.
Control austríaco desde 1706 hasta la oc: Austrian control from 1706 until the Franco-Sarden occupation of 1733.
Convirtió la corte de Nápoles en un impo: He made the court of Naples an important political and cultural center of the Mediterranean. His succession in favor of Joan I opened a stage of conflicts between Angevin branches.
Coronado en vida de Fernando III; no hub: Crowned in the life of Ferdinand III; there was no imperial succession or exclusive authority.
Coronado en vida de Fernando III; no se: Crowned in the life of Fernando III; it is not interpreted as an exclusive succession.
Coronado en vida de su padre en 1170, nu: Crowned in his father's life in 1170, he never ruled for himself: the title is not registered as a command. He rebelled in 1173 and died before Henry II.
Corregencia de Alberto II y Otón; la adq: Corregency of Albert II and Otto; the acquisition does not derive from the imperial office.
Cosimo Migliorati fue el papa de la obed: Cosimo Migliorati was the pope of Roman obedience between 1404 and 1406. A revolt in Rome forced him to take refuge in Viterbo in 1405.
Creado por Enrique VIII para Conn O’Neil: Created by Henry VIII for Conn O’Neill, the earldom was intended to turn Gaelic power into an inherited dignity recognized by the Crown. Matthew’s appointment and his descendants clashed with other members of the lineage. That’s why it has a separate entry from Tir Eoghain.
Criado en el ambiente de la corte persa,: Raised in the Persian court environment, he was installed by Abbas I after the fall of Luarsab II. His authority depended on the safavid presence and was limited outside the centers that he controlled.
Cristoforo Castiglione y Luigia, o Alois: Cristoforo Castiglione and Luigia, or Aloisa, Gonzaga were the parents of Baldassare. The family had its heritage in the area of Mantua and maintained ties with the ruling house of the city.
Cronología tradicional con interrupcione: Traditional chronology with interruptions and rivalry with Radu II; no continuous control is claimed in each month.
Cuarto hijo de Enrique II y Leonor de Aq: Fourth son of Henry II and Leonor of Aquitaine, he ruled Brittany since his marriage to Duchess Constance in 1181. He participated in the rebellions against his father and died in Paris in 1186; his posthumous son Arthur inherited his rights.
Cuatro generaciones de duques reunieron: Four generations of dukes gathered Burgundy and a large group of Dutch principalities before the succession crisis of 1477.
César Borja elimina en Senigallia a vari: Cesare Borgia eliminates in Senigallia several captains who had rebelled against him. The episode, observed by Machiavelli, summarizes the conflict between the territorial prince and the autonomous condotiers.
Cómo Polonia convirtió una monarquía her: How Poland turned a hereditary monarchy into a chosen crown.
David aparece con numeración VII en part: David appears with numbering VII in part of the trapezuntina bibliography; it corresponds to the Georgian monarch named David IX in the Atlas.
David de Escocia, conde de Huntingdon: David of Scotland, Count of Huntingdon
David sucedió a su hermano. La fecha de: David succeeded his brother. The date of 1460 follows the review of contemporary documentation against earlier dates.
De Montgisard a Hattin: victorias, tregu: From Montgisard to Hattin: victories, truces and a fragile succession
De expugnatione Terrae Sanctae per Salad: De espugnatione Terrae Sanctae per Saladinum · testimony of the taking of Jerusalem (1187)
De la oposición a la revuelta: From the Opposition to the Revolt
De las compañías de ventura al ducado de: From the companies of venture to the Duchy of Milan
De los patrimonios croatas a la frontera: From Croatian heritages to the Ottoman border and transylvanic links.
De salvar Viena a pasar a la ofensiva: From saving Vienna to moving on to the offensive
De un linaje condal suabo a la casa que: From a Swabian lineage to the house that brought together the Empire, Austria, Bohemia, Hungary, the Spanish Monarchy and the Netherlands, divided since 1556 into an Austrian and a Spanish branch.
Defendió Ferrara frente a las presiones: He defended Ferrara against the pontifical pressures during the Italian wars. His artillery experience and alliances were essential for the survival of the duchy.
Defendió derechos sobre Güeldres frente: He defended rights over Guelders in front of his sister Mary’s line. The dispute faced two female paths towards the same inheritance. The victory of the supporters of Mary’s son consolidated Jülich’s new ducal house.
Defendió la autonomía de Kartli frente a: He defended Kartli’s autonomy against the safavid campaigns. He died as a result of the battle of Garisi; his son Simon continued the resistance. Sources disagree over a few years of his reign, here between 1527 and 1556.
Defendió la autonomía de su imperio fren: He defended the autonomy of his empire against the tutelage of Andronic II and negotiated commercial access for genoese and Venetians. His marriage to Djiadjak Jakeli reinforced the connection with Samtsje and the Georgian elites.
Defendió los derechos de los Avesnes sob: He defended the rights of the Birds over Henao in front of his half brothers Dampierre. Louis IX’s arbitration supported a distribution of inheritances, but did not immediately eliminate the conflicts. He died before his mother; his son John II continued the line of the county.
Defendió su elección como jefe de los O’: He defended his election as head of the O’Neill against the successor system of Earldom of Tyrone. He alternated war and negotiation with Elizabeth I, and contested the dominance of Northern Ireland over other Gaelic houses.
Defendió sus derechos sobre Artois frent: He defended his rights over Artois against the claims of his nephew Roberto. His political position was reinforced by the marriages of his daughters in the French royal family.
Dependió del respaldo de Mingrelia para: He depended on Mingrelia's backing to attain and regain the throne. His reign included a break during the intervention of Simon of Kartli and his Western rivals, so two mandates are recorded.
Depuesto en 1180; el ducado pasó a Otón: Deposed in 1180; the duchy passed to Otto de Wittelsbach.
Depuesto por la intervención persa y oto: Deposed by the Persian and Ottoman intervention; exit to Russia in 1724.
Depuso a Ricardo II e inauguró la dinast: He deposed Richard II and inaugurated Lancaster dynasty. His reign had to face nobility rebellions and the Welsh uprising of Owin Glynd
Depuso a su hermano Erico XIV y buscó un: He deposed his brother Erico XIV and sought an intermediate religious policy. His marriage to Catherine Jagelón linked the Vasa to the Polish succession.
Derechos adquiridos en 1441; ciudad toma: Rights acquired in 1441; city taken in 1443. Some chronologies date dignity in 1444.
Derechos comprados en 1515; el acuerdo g: Rights purchased in 1515; the general submission agreement was 1524.
Derechos de Veringen, con posteriores de: Veringen's rights, with subsequent rights to Waldburg-Warthausen.
Derechos transmitidos por Margarita de B: Rights transmitted by Margaret of Béarn.
Desde 1512, las dos líneas no gobernaron: Since 1512, the two lines did not effectively govern the entire ancient kingdom.
Desde la elección de Alberto II como rey: Since the election of Albert II as King of the Romans in 1438 and that of Frederick III in 1440, royal and later imperial dignity fell almost without interruption in the house. Frederick III married his son Maximilian to Mary of Burgundy in 1477. Philip the Beautiful's links with Joan of Castile and Maximilian's grandsons with the Jagellon led Charles V and Ferdinand I to gather Castile, Aragon, Italy, the Netherlands, Austria, Bohemia and Hungary. With the abdications of Charles V in 1555–1556, Philip II received the Spanish Monarchy and Ferdinand I remained at the head of the Central European domains; he was recognized emperor in 1558.
Desde septiembre de 1556 administró el I: Since September 1556 he administered the Empire as King of the Romans; the electors accepted in Frankfurt in February 1558 the resignation of Charles V.
Desplazó a su hermano Smbat y ocupó brev: He displaced his brother Smbat and briefly occupied the crown before returning power to Hetum II. His reign was another phase of a dynastic dispute involving several sons of Leo II.
Desplazó a su padre Alejandro II y ocupó: He displaced his father Alexander II and held the throne for about a year. His death allowed Alexander to be restored. Through his wife Ketevan and his son Teimuraz, his line was linked to resistance to Abbas I.
Después de la regencia acordada en Delft: After the regency agreed at Delft, Jacqueline relinquished Holland, Hainaut and Zeeland in 1433.
Destacó en la defensa jacobita durante l: He excelled in Jacobite defense during the Irish War and participated in the negotiation that culminated in the Limerick Treaty. He then went to the French service and died of wounds received in Landen. His county belonged to the nobility created by James II in exile.

Dignidad ducal heredada en 1690, sin rec: Ducal dignity inherited in 1690, without effective recovery from the ducats to Ryswick in 1697.
Dinkelsbühl, Rothenburg, Weißenburg y Sc: Dinkelsbühl, Rothenburg, Weißenburg and Schweinfurt are different urban jurisdictions. Cartographic grouping of imperial cities, without attributing to them a common government.
Diplomático de origen italiano, cardenal: Diplomat of Italian origin, cardinal and chief minister during the regency of Anne of Austria and the youth of Louis XIV. Overcame the Fronda and intervened in the negotiations of Westphalia and peace of the Pyrenees.
Diplomático, funcionario y escritor flor: Diplomat, civil servant and Florentine writer whose political experience was fed by The Prince and the Discourses. He closely observed Caesar Borja and the Italian powers of the early 16th century.
Dirigió la causa realista en Irlanda dur: He led the realistic cause in Ireland during the wars of the three kingdoms and negotiated with the Catholic Confederation. After the Restoration he again exercised the delegated government of the island. His successive dignitaries are distinguished from Count, Marquis and Duke.
Dirigió la rama meridional de los Fitzge: He led the southern branch of the Fitzgerald during the Tudor consolidation. His alliances and conflicts with the Butlers conditioned Munster’s policy. His son Gerald inherited domains that would be the center of Desmond’s rebellions.
Dirigió una red marítima y territorial e: He led a maritime and territorial network on the west coast of Ireland. He negotiated and fought with Tudor authorities and local rivals; his encounter with Isabel I was part of that defense of his interests. His authority did not amount to a crown over Ireland.
Disputa con Luis II de Anjou; conserva u: He disagrees with Louis II of Anjou; he retains a base in Gaeta.
He disputes succession during his minority.
Disputó Connacht a otros miembros de su: Connacht argued with other members of his home and combined Irish alliances with Anglo-Norman agreements. His reign shows the continuity of the Gaelic kingdoms after 1169 and the need to negotiate with the new stately monarchy.
Disputó Güeldres a su hermano Reinaldo I: Guelders opposed his brother Reinald III and displaced him from the government in 1361. His death in 1371 allowed a brief restoration of Reinaldo. The disappearance of both without offspring opened a new dispute between the lines of his sisters.
Disputó la herencia de la monarquía unid: He disputed the heritage of the united monarchy, but eventually recognized the separation of Kajetia and Imereti. His kingdom was centered on Kartli. His sons gave continuity to the royal line and the princely branch of Mukhrani.

Royal descent also passes through the daughters. Philippa, daughter of Lionel, marries Edmund Mortimer, Earl of March. His granddaughter Anne Mortimer will take that ancestry to York. Lands, revenues, kinship and proximity to the king give these branches resources to intervene in the government.

Control of the king’s person allows control of the decisions made on his behalf. Edward is lodged in the Tower of London; then his brother Richard of Shrewsbury meets with him. The Tower is a royal residence and the usual place of preparation for coronations, but the two children are subject to the new division of power. Elizabeth Woodville seeks refuge in Westminster with other members of her family. Edward’s coronation is postponed.

Elector de Sajonia entre 1586 y 1591. Co: Elector of Saxony between 1586 and 1591. With his chancellor Nikolaus Krell he favored an approach to Calvinism that was thrown away after his death.
Elector de Sajonia y rey de Polonia dura: Elector of Saxony and king of Poland during a period of growing political paralysis of the Commonwealth. His reign reinforced the dynastic connection between Dresden and Warsaw.
Elector de Sajonia, 1763–1763. Elector d: Elector of Saxony, 1763–1763. Elector of the Wettin dynasty.
Elector del Palatinado y, durante el inv: Elector of the Palatinate and, during the winter of 1619–1620, king of Bohemia. His acceptance of the Bohemian crown turned a constitutional crisis into one of the triggers of the Thirty Years' War.
Elector desde 1559, impulsó el calvinism: Since 1559, he has promoted Calvinism in the Palatinate. His son Louis VI has changed confessional politics again.
Electress consort of the Medici dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Tuscany, Palatinate.
Electora de la dinastía Wittelsbach. Su: Voter of the Wittelsbach dynasty. Her trajectory is linked to Palatinate, Hanover.
Elegida sucesora de su marido Gabriel Be: Elected successor to her husband Gabriel Bethlen, she ruled briefly in her own right. Her resignation in 1630 shows the limits that the estates and factions imposed on princely power; it was not only a consort.
Elegido como sucesor del emperador Ferna: Chosen as successor to Emperor Ferdinand III; he died before his father and did not reach emperor.
Chosen during his captivity in Genoa.
Elegido o coronado en vida del predeceso: Chosen or crowned in the life of the predecessor; non-exclusive authority.
Elegido rey en 1292 tras el arbitraje de: Elected king in 1292 after Edward I of England's arbitration in the Great Cause. Deposed in 1296 at the beginning of the open phase of the wars of independence.
Elegido voivoda de Transilvania, pasó a: Elected voivode of Transylvania, he became king in Poland and preserved the dignity of Prince Transylvanus. His brother Christopher administered the territory as voivode. The distinction between these charges avoids presenting two rival successions where there was a distribution of government.
Emilio Altieri fue elegido en 1670, con: Emilio Altieri was elected in 1670, almost eighty years old, and his adopted nephew, Cardinal Paluzzo Altieri, led the government until his death in 1676.
Emperador Habsburgo asociado al despotis: Emperor Habsburg associated with enlightened despotism. He tried to thoroughly modernize the administration, the Church and society of his territories through a very ambitious reform program.
Emperador Habsburgo cuya política matrim: Emperor Habsburg whose marriage policy laid the foundations for the extraordinary dynastic expansion of his home through Europe.
Emperador Habsburgo de breve reinado, su: Emperor Habsburg of brief reign, succeeded after governing Tuscany. He moderated several reforms by Joseph II and faced the expansion of the French Revolution in Europe.
Emperador Habsburgo de larguísimo reinad: Emperor Habsburg of a very long reign that preserved and patiently extended the interests of his home. His son Maximilian's marriage to Mary of Burgundy transformed the future of the dynasty.
Emperador Habsburgo de perfil relativame: Emperor Habsburg of a relatively conciliatory profile in a Europe divided by the Reformation. He also ruled Bohemia and Hungary within the complex Central European monarchy of his home.
Emperador Habsburgo durante casi medio s: Emperor Habsburg for almost half a century. His reign was marked by the wars against Louis XIV and by the great confrontation with the Ottoman Empire culminated in Vienna in 1683.
Emperador Habsburgo durante la Guerra de: Emperor Habsburg during the Spanish War of Succession. He continued the policy of his father Leopold I and supported the candidacy of his brother Charles to the Spanish throne.
Emperador Habsburgo que arrebató progres: Emperor Habsburg who progressively seized power from his brother Rodolfo II. His reign prepared the successor and religious crisis that would lead to the Thirty Years' War.
Emperador Habsburgo que trasladó su cort: Emperor Habsburg who moved his court to Prague and brought together artists, astronomers and scholars. His political and religious difficulties weakened his authority over other members of the dynasty.
Emperador Habsburgo y ferviente defensor: Emperor Habsburg and fervent defender of Catholicism. Bohemia’s rebellion against its authority triggered the Thirty Years’ War, which transformed the political map of the Holy Roman Empire.
Emperador Habsburgo y rival de Felipe V: Emperor Habsburg and rival of Philip V in the War of Succession. His house ruled Milan, Naples and Sardinia on different dates; he exchanged Sardinia for Sicily in 1720. The Pragmatic Sanction sought to secure his inheritance to Mary Theresa.
Emperador Hohenstaufen, rey de Sicilia y: Emperor Hohenstaufen, king of Sicily and Jerusalem, an exceptional figure of the Mediterranean policy of the thirteenth century. His conflict with the papacy and his Sicilian court marked an entire epoch.
Emperador bizantino desde 1195 tras derr: Byzantine Emperor since 1195 after overthrowing and blinding his brother Isaac II. He fled Constantinople at the arrival of the fourth crusade in 1203.
Emperador bizantino desde 1328 tras una: Byzantine Emperor since 1328 after a civil war against his grandfather Andronic II. He lost almost all of Asia Minor to the Ottomans, but recovered Thessaly and Epirus.
Emperador bizantino desde 1391. Viajó po: Byzantine Emperor since 1391. Traveled through Western Europe seeking help against the Ottomans; Bayezid's defeat to Tamerlan in 1402 gave Constantinople a break.
Emperador bizantino durante medio siglo: Byzantine emperor during half a century of civil wars, first against John VI Cantacuceno and then before his son Andronic IV. His empire was reduced and taxed by the Ottomans.
Emperador de Nicea desde 1221. Amplió el: Emperor of Nicea since 1221. He expanded the status of Nicen in Asia Minor and the Balkans and prepared for the recovery of Constantinople. The Orthodox Church venerates him as saint.
Emperador de Nicea entre 1254 y 1258, hi: Emperor of Nicaea between 1254 and 1258, son of John III Vatatzés. Erudite and author of theological works, he died young leaving a younger son, John IV.
Emperador de Rusia e hijo de Catalina II: Emperor of Russia and son of Catherine II. He tried to reorganize succession and court discipline, but his authoritarian rule ended with his murder in 1801.
Emperador de la casa de Luxemburgo y rey: Emperor of the house of Luxembourg and king of Bohemia, he made Prague one of the great political and cultural centres of Europe. The Golden Bull of 1356 ordered the imperial election in a lasting way.
Emperador de la casa de Wittelsbach cuya: Emperor of the house of Wittelsbach whose struggle for the German crown led to a prolonged conflict with the papacy. His reign reflected the political fracture of the Holy Roman Empire in the 14th century.
Emperador del Sacro Imperio y soberano d: Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire and sovereign of a composite monarchy that reached the Iberian peninsula, Italy, the Netherlands and America. Philip I inherited the Franche-Comté, Artois, Namur and Luxembourg, as well as other Dutch territories. He later incorporated Frisia, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drente, Groningen and Guelders in a staggered form, between 1524 and 1543. He preserved the ducal dignity of Burgundy, but did not rule the Duchy incorporated into France. From 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; the investiture and subsequent possession of Philip II must be distinguished from that government.
Emperador durante la fase final de la Gu: Emperor during the final phase of the Thirty Years' War. Participated in the negotiation of the political order that culminated in the Peace of Westphalia of 1648.
Emperador latino de Constantinopla desde: Latin Emperor of Constantinople since 1221, from the house of Courtenay. He lost much of his territory to Nicaea and Epirus.
Emperador menor junto a Miguel VIII; no: Minor Emperor with Michael VIII; not independent authority over another empire.
Emperador niño de Nicea desde 1258. Migu: Emperor boy of Nicaea since 1258. Michael VIII Paleologist, his co-regent, removed him after regaining Constantinople in 1261 and ordered blinding him.
Emperador ruso de brevísimo reinado. Su: Russian Emperor of a very brief reign. His admiration for Frederick II altered Russian foreign policy and his rapid fall opened the way to the power of Catherine II.
Emperatriz de Rusia desde 1730, sobrina: Empress of Russia since 1730, niece of Peter the Great. He broke the conditions that the nobility wanted to impose on him and ruled with German favorites such as Biron.
Emperatriz de Rusia durante una gran exp: Empress of Russia during a great territorial and political expansion. Her reign combined enlightened ideas, nobility strengthening and an active European policy.
Emperatriz de Rusia e hija de Pedro el G: Empress of Russia and daughter of Peter the Great. Her reign consolidated the European position of the empire and was marked by Russian participation in the Seven Years War.
En 1157 reconoció la soberanía de Ramón: In 1157 he recognized the sovereignty of Ramón Berenguer IV of Barcelona.
En 1167 reconoció la soberanía de Alfons: In 1167 he recognized the sovereignty of Alfonso II of Aragon.
En 1213 juró fidelidad a Pedro II de Ara: In 1213 he swore allegiance to Peter II of Aragon. The Lateran Council dispossessed him in 1215 in favor of Simon of Montfort; he recovered Toulouse in 1217.
En 1213 rindió homenaje a Pedro II de Ar: In 1213 he paid homage to Pedro II of Aragon for his castles and fought alongside him in Muret.
In 1213 he paid homage to Pedro II of Aragon for his castles.
En 1468 nombró a su hijo Fernando rey y: In 1468 he appointed his son Ferdinand king and co-regent of Sicily; he retained the crown until his death.
En 1620 entró en Pau y proclamó el edict: In 1620 he entered Pau and proclaimed the edict of the bond of the Bearne to France.
En 1801 cede a Francia los territorios p: In 1801, the Palatine territories of the left bank of the Rhine, which had been occupied for years, were ceded to France; it remained on the right bank until the rearrangement of 1803.
En Mesina se concentra una armada hetero: In Messina, a heterogeneous army of Spaniards, Venetians, pontificals, genoese and other Italian contingents is concentrated. Coordinating different interests is almost as important as gathering the ships.
En el centro, la galera Real de don Juan: In the centre, the Royal Gallery of Don Juan and the Sultan of Ali Bajá are locked in a struggle of approaches, archabuces and successive reinforcements. Ali Bajá's fall and the taking of his ship disorganize the Ottoman center and make central combat the symbolic nucleus of victory.
En febrero de 1461, Eduardo derrota a la: In February 1461, Edward defeated Jasper Tudor’s forces at Mortimer’s Cross, along the Welsh border. Owen Tudor, Jasper’s father and grandfather of Henry Tudor, was captured and was executed. War thus reached the Welsh branch related to Henry VI through Catherine of Valois. Margaret meanwhile obtained a victory in the second battle of Saint Albans and recovered the king. But her troops encountered political resistance and supply problems on the way to London. Edward met with Warwick and entered the capital. There he was recognized as Edward IV in early March. The decision would have to withstand the Lancastrian army concentrated in Yorkshire.
En julio, el ejército del reino marcha h: In July, the army of the kingdom marches towards Tiberias and remains in a critical situation of heat, harassment and access to water. The defeat of July 4th in Hattin leaves leaders prisoners and destroys much of the force that could help the cities. The cities retain their fortifications, but they lack the necessary men and resources to defend them. The loss of the army hinders the relief of the cities and accelerates the conquests of Saladin during the following months.
En junio se declara inválido el matrimon: In June Edward IV’s marriage to Elizabeth Woodville was declared invalid, claiming a previous marriage commitment by the king. His sons were excluded and Richard accepted the crown. He was crowned in July with Anne Neville. The law known as Titulus Regius would confirm the following year this justification for his accession. The two princes ceased to appear in public; their fate and the date of their death remained unknown. Part of Edward IV’s former supporters turned against Richard. The Duke of Buckingham’s rebellion failed in the autumn of 1483, but enabled the convergence of Yorkist opponents and defenders of Henry Tudor. Margaret Beaufort and Elizabeth Woodville favoured a marriage project between Henry and Elizabeth of York. The death of Edward of Middleham in 1484 left Richard without his legitimate son.
En plena Guerra de Sucesión Austríaca, e: In the midst of the Austrian War of Succession, elector Wittelsbach Charles Albert obtains the imperial crown and demonstrates that dignity remains elective, even after centuries of Habsburg predominance.
Encabezó a los Butler durante la expansi: He led the Butlers during the Tudor administrative expansion. His marriage to Joan FitzGerald linked two of Ireland’s great rival houses. His son Thomas would become one of Isabel I’s main supporters in Munster.
Encabezó la rebelión de 1534 tras recibi: He led the rebellion in 1534 after receiving news of his father’s fate. The defeat and execution in London ended the immediate hegemony of the Kildare. The subsequent restoration of his half brother preserved the continuity of the lineage.

Enrique III es asesinado después de habe: Henry III is killed after having allied with Henry of Navarre against the League. With his death the Valois-Angulema line on the throne is extinguished and Henry of Navarre claims the crown as Henry IV.
Enrique IV promulga el Edicto de Nantes: Henry IV promulgates the Edict of Nantes and grants Protestants civil rights and a limited framework of worship and security. The Bourbon monarchy closes the great phase of the Wars of Religion without imposing complete confessional uniformity.
Enrique Tudor une dos genealogías difere: Henry Tudor joins two different genealogies. Through his father Edmund he descends from Owen Tudor and Catherine of Valois, the widow of Henry V. His blood connection with Edward III comes from his mother, Margaret Beaufort: she is the daughter of John, Duke of Somerset; this was the son of John Beaufort, Count of Somerset, born of John of Gaunt and Catherine of Roet. The Beauforts were legitimized after their parents' marriage; a later confirmation by Henry IV included an exclusion from the royal succession. The strength of the Tudor candidacy grows thanks to the support of Lancaster survivors and the alliance promised with Elizabeth of York. Henry has been in exile for years and needs to convert that coalition into an army capable of conquering England.
Enrique VI ha heredado la corona siendo: Henry VI has inherited the crown as a baby. His marriage to Margaret of Anjou was intended to favour a settlement with France, but the loss of Normandy in 1450 and Gascony in 1453 discredits his advisors. Debt, the distribution of offices and the return of men linked to the war fuel the disputes. Richard of York, who has held command in France and Ireland, accuses rivals like the Duke of Somerset of mismanaging the government. In 1453 the king suffers a disease that prevents him from exercising power. In October his son Edward of Westminster is born. Margaret defends the interests of the child while the council and the great lords seek who will be able to rule. The future minority of the heir and the present incapacity of the king make the organization of the regency a decisive struggle.
Enrique VI vuelve al trono: Henry VI returns to the throne
Enrique VII del Sacro Imperio: Henry VII of the Holy Roman Empire
Enrique VII se corona en octubre de 1485: Henry VII was crowned in October 1485 and married Elizabeth of York in January 1486. Edward IV’s daughter brought to the new reign the ancestry of the Yorkist branch and the support of those who defended her family. Arthur, heir of both lines, was born in September. The Tudor rose, which brings together the colors red and white, makes marriage an image of harmony. Henry governs by means of rewards, agreements, monitoring of the great magnate networks and punishments to his adversaries. Marriage links family inheritances, while the preservation of the throne requires administering resources and neutralizing new rebellions.
Enrique de Bolingbroke regresa del exili: Henry of Bolingbroke returns from exile after Richard II takes possession of his father’s inheritance, John of Gaunt. Opposition to the king turns a claim to an inheritance into a change of monarch. Richard is deposed and Henry reigns as Henry IV. His son Henry V strengthens the new dynasty with his French campaigns. The deposition leaves an open question: other descendants of Edward III may regard their claim by descent as stronger. Richard of York descends from Edmund of Langley by his father and Lionel of Antwerp by his mother, Anne Mortimer. This second line will allow him to invoke an ancestry prior to that of Lancasters. The genealogical argument will acquire political force when royal authority fails.
Enrique de Escocia, conde de Northumbria: Henry of Scotland, Earl of Northumbria
Enrique desembarca en Gales en agosto de: Henry disembarks in Wales in August 1485 and marches towards the center of England. Richard gathers an army to close his way. On August 22 they face off in Bosworth. Stanleys have their own forces and hold a decisive position: Thomas Stanley is the husband of Margaret Beaufort, Henry’s mother, but retains ties and obligations with Richard. William Stanley’s intervention against the king turns the battle. Richard leads a charge towards Henry’s position and dies fighting. Victory opens the throne to the Tudor claimant. His allies include Lancaster supporters, former servants of Edward IV and men who have changed sides during the crisis. Henry will have to hold that coalition together once the campaign is over.
Enrique el Piadoso sucedió en 1539 a su: Henry the Pious succeeded in 1539 his brother George in the Albertine Saxony and introduced the Lutheran Reformation there.
Entidad regional con sus fases, relacion: Regional entity with its phases, relations of superiority and sources located in the cartographic review. Tax dependence does not amount to direct provincial administration; an occupation does not change its identity by itself.
Entregó la administración del Imperio a: He handed over the administration of the Empire to his brother Ferdinand in September 1556.
Episodio de enero–junio seguido de resta: January–June episode followed by Borbonic restoration; Napoli's cell as a disputed annual summary.
Erik Klipping, rey de Dinamarca desde 12: Erik Klipping, king of Denmark since 1259. He had to accept in 1282 a letter limiting royal power and was assassinated in 1286.
Eschiva de Ibelin, señora de Beirut: Eschiva of Ibelin, madame of Beirut
Escritor, humanista y diplomático de la: Writer, humanist and diplomat of the court of Urbino, author of El cortano, published in 1528. He served Gonzaga and the Dukes of Urbino and was nuncio of Clement VII to Charles V. He died in Toledo in 1529.
Escritora nacida en Venecia y formada en: She was born in Venice and trained in the French court. She composed poetry and political and moral treatises, and defended the intellectual capacity and dignity of women in The City of Ladies, written in 1405.
Esposa de Alain de Albret, fue madre de: Wife of Alain de Albret, she was the mother of John III of Navarre and Charlotte of Albret. Her offspring connect the French nobility heritages with the Navarren monarchy and the Borja. Her birth year is preserved as approximate, avoiding presenting a conventional figure as an exact date.
Esposa de Alejo IV, fue madre de Juan IV: Wife of Alejo IV, she was the mother of John IV and David. Her identity must be distinguished from the same-named empress married to Alejo III. Registering both unions as one would produce an impossible genealogy.
Esposa de Baldassare Castiglione desde 1: Wife of Baldassare Castiglione since 1516. Her death in 1520 preceded the ecclesiastical stage and the Spanish nunciature of her husband.
Esposa de Gastón II y madre de Gastón Fé: Wife of Gaston II and mother of Gastón Fébus, he intervened in the government of family heritage during the minority of his son. His trajectory allows us to observe the role of mothers of minor heirs in political continuity.
Esposa de Guillermo II de Sicilia (1177): Wife of William II of Sicily (1177) and, after widowing and accompanying his brother Richard in the crusade, Raimundo VI of Toulouse (1196).
Esposa de Guillermo IX, ejerció la tutel: Wife of William IX, he exercised the tutelage of his son Bonifacio IV and defended the interests of the Paleologists during the Italian wars. He also intervened in the marriage negotiations that ended up uniting his daughter Margarita with Frederick II Gonzaga.
Esposa de Jorge II Rákóczi y madre de Fr: Wife of George II Rákóczi and mother of Francis I, he maintained a decisive position in the family domains after the crisis of the principality. His intervention contributed to the forgiveness of his son after the conspiracy of 1670. Francis' wedding with Jelena Zrinski extended that network to Croatia.
Esposa de Juan III Sobieski y reina de P: Wife of John III Sobieski and queen of Poland, influenced the politics of the court and the succession. After the death of the king he lived in Rome and then in France, where he died in 1716.
Esposa de León II y madre de una amplia: Wife of Leo II and mother of a large royal offspring, she appears with her family in a famous image of Armenian manuscript. Her children occupied the crown or established links with Byzantium and Cyprus, giving this generation a great Mediterranean projection.
Esposa de Pedro I y madre de Pedro II, d: Wife of Peter I and mother of Peter II, he played a prominent political role after the murder of her husband. He intervened in the court struggles and in his relations with Genoa. He ended up returning to the dominions of the Crown of Aragon.
Esposa de Pedro el Grande y primera muje: Wife of Peter the Great and first woman to rule Russia as Empress. His brief reign ensured immediate political continuity after the death of Peter I.
Esposa de Stefan Branković, compartió el: Stefan Branković’s wife shared the family’s displacement after the loss of Serbian power. Her sons Đorđe and Jovan retained the dignity of despot in the Hungarian sphere. Her religious memory became associated with Krušedol and with preserving the dynasty’s tradition in exile.
Esposa de Sten Sture el Joven. Tras la m: Wife of Sten Sture the Younger. After the death of her husband in 1520 she led the Stockholm resistance against Cristian II and negotiated his capitulation. She was imprisoned after the conquest. Her son Svante extended the presence of the Sture in the nobility of the Swedish Vasa.
Esposa del rey Juan e hija de la casa de: Wife of King John and daughter of Wettin's house. He defended Stockholm during the Swedish rebellion of 1501 and was imprisoned after the capitulation. He was the mother of Cristian II: his experience illustrates the fragility of the common government before the last attempt to preserve the union.
Esposo de María de Sicilia e hijo de Mar: Husband of Mary of Sicily and son of Martin the Human. He reorganized the power of the island monarchy in front of the barons and died after a campaign in Sardinia. His death without a legitimate surviving heir aggravated the succession of the Crown of Aragon.
Esposo de Sibila y rey de Jerusalén dura: Husband of Sibila and king of Jerusalem during Hattin’s defeat. After losing the capital, he continued the struggle and ended up establishing Lusignan power in Cyprus.
Esta agrupación permite explorar un espa: This grouping allows exploring a space of republics, principalities, fiefs and kingdoms. It does not represent a single Italian state nor does it admit a common succession of sovereigns.
Esta entrada reúne los registros de la r: This entry gathers the records of Germanic or Roman royalty. The election as King of the Romans and imperial dignity did not always have the same dates nor immediately fell into the same person.
Estatúder de Países Bajos, 1640–1664 (go: Statuer of the Netherlands, 1640–1664 (delegated government).Prince of the Nassau dynasty.
Estatúder de Países Bajos, 1647–1650 (go: Statuer of the Netherlands, 1647–1650 (delegated government). Prince of Orange of the Nassau dynasty.
Expandió el poder de Connacht y disputó: He expanded Connacht’s power and contested Irish supremacy to other regional dynasties. His sons Ruaidrí and Cathal represent two successive responses to the political change of the 12th century.
Extinción de la casa y guerra de Zúrich;: Extinction of the house and war of Zurich; inheritance of the Raron in 1437/1440.
Fabio Chigi se convierte en Alejandro VI: Fabio Chigi becomes Alexander VII and calls his family to Rome; his nephew Flavio occupies the traditional place of the cardinal-nepote.
Fabio Chigi, sienés y nuncio en Münster: Fabio Chigi, Sienese and Nuncio in Münster during the Westphalia negotiations, was pope between 1655 and 1667. He commissioned Bernini the colonnade of St. Peter’s Square and received Cristina from Sweden in Rome.

Federico Diente de Hierro, elector de Br: Frederick Iron Tooth, elector of Brandenburg between 1440 and 1470. He subjected the cities of Berlin and Cölln and recovered in 1455 the New Mark from the hands of the Teutonic Order.
Federico I del Sacro Imperio: Frederick I of the Holy Roman Empire
Federico I, llamado Barbarroja, fue rey: Frederick I, called Barbarossa, was King of the Romans since 1152 and emperor since 1155. From the house of Hohenstaufen, he disputed power in Italy and participated in the Third Crusade. He left for land in 1189 and died drowned in the Saleph River on June 10, 1190, before arriving in the Holy Land. He was the father of Philip of Swabia.
Federico II recupera Jerusalén por trata: Frederick II recovers Jerusalem by treaty

Federico de Hesse-Kassel, rey de Suecia: Frederick of Hesse-Kassel, king of Sweden since 1720 for the abdication of his wife Ulrica Leonor. He reigned during the so-called era of Freedom, with a real power very limited by parliament; since 1730 he was also Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel.
Federico el Sabio, elector de Sajonia de: Frederick the Wise, Elector of Saxony since 1486. He founded Wittenberg University (1502) and protected Martin Luther, whom he had hidden in the castle of Wartburg after the Diet of Worms (1521).
Felipe Melanchthon presenta ante Carlos: Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of Lutheran faith, supported by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Felipe de Valois, duque de Orleans: Philip of Valois, Duke of Orleans
Felipe el Bueno funda la Orden del Toisó: Philip the Good founds the Order of the Golden Toison in the context of his marriage to Isabella of Portugal.

Fernando Carlos heredó Tirol en 1632 sie: Ferdinand Charles inherited Tirol in 1632 as a child. His mother Claudia de Medici ruled as regent until 1646; then he exercised power personally until his death in 1662.

Fernando Álvarez de Toledo, III duque de: Fernando Álvarez de Toledo, 3rd Duke of Alba, was governor general of the Netherlands by Philip II between 1567 and 1573. His repressive policy and the campaigns of revolt marked the government.
Ferrandino, rey de Nápoles entre 1495 y: Ferrandino, king of Naples between 1495 and 1496. He fled before the invasion of Charles VIII of France and recovered the kingdom with Spanish and Venetian help, but died the following year without children.
Ferrante, hijo natural de Alfonso V de A: Ferrante, natural son of Alfonso V of Aragon, king of Naples since 1458. He overcame the revolt of the Barons of 1485 with harshness and was a central actor of Italian equilibrium.
Feudo concedido a Leonardo Cubello en 14: Feud granted to Leonardo Cubello in 1410, distinct from Arborea's sovereign judicial dignity. Confiscation and royal reinstatement in 1478.
Figura como Juan V o Juan VI según se in: Figured as John V or John VI according to the inclusion of John of Montfort, pretender of 1341–1345, in the ducal numbering. Both forms designate the same person.
Filiberto II murió sin descendencia. Lo: Filiberto II died without offspring. He was succeeded by his half brother Charles, son of Philip II's second marriage.
Fin del gobierno territorial eclesiástic: End of ecclesiastical territorial government, after the interval of the atlas.
Flandes, Artois y el Franco Condado se s: Flanders, Artois and the Franche-Comté joined by Margaret's hereditary right; their children received Nevers and Rethel as apanages before 1405.
Fortaleció el ejército y la administraci: He strengthened the Hungarian army and administration and disputed territories to the Habsburgs and the Jagellons. His library and court made Buddha a center of Renaissance humanism.
Fortaleció la administración del princip: He strengthened the administration of the principality and intervened in the Thirty Years' War against the Habsburgs. He was elected king of Hungary, but renounced that claim in the peace of Nikolsburg; his marriage to Catherine of Brandenburg brought him closer to the Protestant powers.
Fraile. Su trayectoria está vinculada a: Fraile, his trajectory is linked to the Holy Roman Empire.

Heredera del señorío de Beirut, perdió s: Heir of the lordship of Beirut, he lost his territorial base with the Mamluk conquest. Married to Guy of Lusignan, he was the mother of Hugo IV of Cyprus. His trajectory connects the loss of the continental states with the continuity of their families on the island.
Heredera del vizcondado de Bearne, se de: He inherited the Viscounty of Bearne, declared himself vassal of Alfonso II of Aragon and in 1170 married the Catalan noble Guillermo de Moncada, who died in 1172. He was mother of the Viscounts Gastón VI and Guillermo Ramón, with whom the dynasty of the Moncada began in Bearne.
Heredero de Roberto de Nápoles, murió an: Heir to Roberto of Naples, he died before his father. That death caused the succession to fall on his daughters Juana and Maria; his descendants later led the struggles between the branches of the house of Anjou.
Heredero de la corona tras la muerte de: Crown heir to the crown after the death of Corrado IV. Minor in Germany, with Manfredo ruling as Baiulus until crowning in 1258; Conradino's claim does not prove personal government in Sicily.
Heredó Brabante siendo menor, bajo el go: He inherited Brabant as a minor, under the rule of his mother Adelaide. In 1267 he renounced the duchy and the succession passed to his brother Juan I. His brief stage avoids turning the relay from Henry III to John I into an immediate continuity that did not occur.
Heredó Brabante y se casó con Jacoba de: He inherited Brabant and married Jacqueline of Bavaria. The marriage drew him into the conflict over Holland, Zeeland and Hainaut, but did not permanently unite those inheritances. He was succeeded by his brother Philip of Saint-Pol.
Heredó Castilla siendo niño y su minoría: He inherited Castile as a child and his minority was under the influence of the Lara. His accidental death allowed the succession of Berenguela and, through her, Fernando III.
Heredó Flandes y Henao de su hermana Jua: He inherited Flanders and Henao from his sister Joan. The children of his two marriages, Avesnes and Dampierre, disputed the distribution of inheritances. The separation of both successions gave Henao and Flanders different family paths before joining the Borgoñón group.
Heredó Foix y Bearne siendo niño y fue p: He inherited Foix and Bearne as a child and was the father of Gastón Fébus. His marriage to Leonor de Comminges connected the Foix to another house in the Pyrenean realm. His death in 1343 opened the minority of his son, during which Leonor had a role of government.
Heredó Henao, Holanda y Zelanda de su pa: He inherited Henao, Holland and Zeeland from his father and defended his rights against John of Bavaria and Philip the Good. His marriages were part of that political struggle. Delft's agreement of 1428 restricted his power and the 1433 cession incorporated the counties into the Burgundian heritage.
Heredó Holanda siendo niño y desarrolló: He inherited Holland as a child and developed a policy that reinforced the Earl power and its relations with the cities. His murder opened a stage of instability. His son John I’s brief government was followed by the transmission of the heritage to the Avesnes.
Heredó Jülich y Berg de Wolfgang Guiller: He inherited Jülich and Berg from Wolfgang Guillermo in 1653 and succeeded in the electoral Palatinate in 1685. The coincidence in one person did not automatically merge the ducats with the Kurpfalz.
Heredó Monferrato de Bonifacio III y se: He inherited Monferrato de Boniface III and married Anne of Alençon. Her children Margarita and Bonifacio would occupy different positions in the succession: he inherited the marquisate; she transmitted the rights that would end up holding his incorporation into the heritage of Gonzaga.
Heredó Navarra a través de su madre, Bla: He inherited Navarre through his mother, Blanca, linking the kingdom to the county house of Champagne. He was also a prominent poet of the French trovador tradition.
Heredó Navarra siendo menor de edad, baj: He inherited Navarre as a minor, under the regency of his mother Magdalene of France. His premature death led to the succession of his sister Catherine.
Heredó Nápoles de Roberto y enfrentó una: He inherited Roberto's Naples and faced a crisis after the murder of her husband Andrés de Anjou. The invasions of Louis of Hungary, the power of her second husband Louis of Taranto and his election of Louis de Anjou as heir turned the Neapolitan succession into a European conflict.
Heredó de Manfredo III durante su minorí: He inherited from Manfredo III during his minority and made Saluzzo a more stable political center of the marquisate. His mother, Beatrice of Savoy, later married Manfredo of Sicily.

He inherited from Manfredo III during his minority and made Saluzzo a more stable political center of the marquisate. His mother, Beatrice of Savoy, later married Manfredo of Sicily. For that second marriage, Thomas was half brother of Constance of Sicily: a direct connection between the Alps and later Aragonese royalty.
Heredó de su padre Felipe II y se casó c: He inherited from his father Philip II and married Margaret of Austria. The link brought Savoy closer to the Habsburgs and the Netherlands.
Heredó el condado por su madre, María de: He inherited the county by his mother, Marie de Bourbon-Soissons.
Heredó el ducado de Milán siendo niño, p: He inherited the Duchy of Milan as a child, but the power remained in the hands of his uncle Ludovico. The distance between his title and his effective authority is essential to understand the succession of the Sforza.
Heredó el ducado de su hermano Filiberto: He inherited the duchy of his brother Filiberto I. His marriage to Blanche of Montferrat reinforced Savoy's expectations of the Palaeologists' heritage, while the intervention in Saluzzo confronted him with French interests.
Heredó el reino siendo menor y quedó som: He inherited the kingdom as a minor and was subjected to the struggles of the great lords. His marriage to Martin the Younger and the expedition of 1392 restored the royal power with Aragonese support, without erasing the identity of the island crown.
Heredó este condado de Felipe I; Senlis: He inherited this county of Philip I; Senlis had restored it to the house of Austria in 1493.
Heredó la causa de su padre, Juan de Mon: He inherited the cause of his father, Juan de Montfort, and ended up imposing himself after the battle of Auray. Guerande’s agreement consolidated his ducal position.
Heredó la corona continental mientras es: He inherited the continental crown while he was captive to the Aragonese. His liberation, marriage diplomacy and agreements with James II and Frederick articulated the Angioinian attempts to recover Sicily. His sons extended the family to Hungary, Tarento and Durazzo.
Heredó la corona de Carlos III durante l: He inherited the crown of Charles III during the minority age and disputed the kingdom to Louis II of Anjou. His mother Margaret's regency ensured the continuity of the house of Durazzo; later extended his intervention to the politics of Rome.
Heredó la corona de Juan II y la defendi: He inherited the crown of John II and defended it in front of his half brother James. After losing his last bastion he went into exile and maintained his dynastic rights, which would end up linked to Savoy. His effective government is distinguished from his subsequent claim.
Heredó la corona francesa durante la cru: He inherited the French crown during the crusade in which Louis IX died. His intervention against the Crown of Aragon ended in a disastrous campaign and in his own death.
Heredó la corona siendo menor tras el as: He inherited the crown as a minor after the murder of his father. The war with Genoa ended with the loss of Famagusta and burdensome obligations for the monarchy. He died without surviving offspring, so that his uncle James succeeded him.
Heredó la corona siendo niña y fue objet: He inherited the crown as a child and was the subject of disputes over control of the kingdom. His first marriage to Philip of Antioch ended violently; the subsequent liaison with Hetum consolidated a new dynasty. His own rights are preserved in succession.
Heredó la corona siendo niño, bajo una r: He inherited the crown as a child, under a regency that accumulated great power. His search for Latino help and struggles with nobility aggravated instability. He died without an heir to maintain the male line of the Hetúmidas.
Heredó la influencia de su padre y ejerc: He inherited the influence of his father and repeatedly exercised the delegated government of Ireland. Henry VIII’s distrust of his power ended in his arrest. His son Thomas’ rebellion precipitated the collapse of the family position.
Heredó la monarquía de Tamar, pero los p: He inherited Tamar's monarchy, but the first clashes with the Mongols changed the prospects for the expansion of the kingdom. His death left a younger son, David, and the crown passed to his sister Rusudan.
Heredó la reunificación impulsada por Jo: He inherited the reunification promoted by George V. His reign coincided with the black plague and a change in regional balance after the weakening of the Iljanate. His son Bagrat V continued the royal line.
Heredó los derechos de los Hohenstaufen: He inherited the rights of the Hohenstaufen in Germany and Sicily in full struggle with the papacy. His death left Conrado, known as Conradino, as heir to a threatened cause.
Heredó los derechos de su hermano Mateo: He inherited the rights of his brother Matthew and was the figure who sustained Foix's patrimonial continuity by passing to the descendants of the Grailly. Her husband Archambaud participated in the government for that marriage.
Heredó los derechos sobre Bretaña y fue: He inherited rights over Brittany and was queen consort for his marriage to Francis I. The transmission of his inheritance contributed to the union of the duchy with the French crown.
Heredó los ducados de la Corona. Nerio A: He inherited the ducats of the Crown. Nerius Acciaiuoli took Athens in 1388; the court represents full years.
Heredó los ducados de su primo Federico: He inherited the ducats of his cousin Frederick I. He ruled them from Sicily with vicars general.
Heredó siendo niño y se convirtió en el: He inherited as a child and became the first Duke of Savoy in 1416. The elevation of rank did not create a new dynasty.
Heredó siendo niño, con una regencia en: He inherited as a child, with a regency in which his half-brother Valerano stood out. His long-standing government kept Saluzzo between the Saudi pressures and French protection.
Heredó un ducado ocupado en gran parte p: He inherited a duchy largely occupied by other powers. His service to Charles V and Philip II, and especially the victory of San Quintin, contributed to the territorial recovery agreed upon at Cateau-Cambresis.
Herencia de María de Borgoña; la regenci: Inheritance of Mary of Burgundy; the regency preceded her personal government.
Herencia de María de Borgoña; no es el d: Inheritance of Mary of Burgundy; not the French Duchy of Burgundy.
Hermana de Carlos XII, fue reconocida re: Sister of Charles XII, she was recognized Queen of Sweden in 1719 in exchange for accepting a constitution that limited royal power. In 1720 she abdicated in favor of her husband, Frederick of Hesse-Kassel.
Hermana de Guillermo I y Reinaldo IV de: Sister of William I and Reinald IV of Guelders, she was the mother of Mary of Arkel. Her offspring explain the claim of Arnold of Egmond in 1423. The succession was not a direct relationship of father and son between Reinaldo and Arnoldo.
Hermana de Guillermo de Holanda, se casó: Sister of William of Holland, she married John of Avesnes. Through her, their son John II was related to the comital house of Holland. That connection proved decisive in 1299, when the death of John I of Holland allowed the inheritances of Holland and Hainaut to be united.
Hermana de Magnus Eriksson e hija de Ing: Sister of Magnus Eriksson and daughter of Ingeborg of Norway. She married Albert II of Mecklenburg. His son Albert was king of Sweden, while the offspring of his son Henry led to Erik of Pomerania. It is a key connection between Bjälbo, Mecklenburg and the Kalmar union.
Hermana del zar búlgaro Iván Alejandro y: Sister of the Bulgarian Tsar Ivan Alexander and wife of Esteban Dušan of Serbia. He was regent by his son Esteban Uroš V and ended his days as a nun.
Hermana y heredera de Bohemundo VII, reg: Sister and heiress of Bohemundo VII, he returned from Italy to claim Tripoli. He had to negotiate with the commune and Genoa before the conquest of Qalawun in 1289 ended with the Latin county.

Hermano de Alejandro V, ocupó el trono d: Brother of Alexander V, he held the throne during another interruption of his government. The competition between the princes of this generation continued later in the rivalry of his son Teimuraz with Solomon I.
Hermano de Amadeo IV, recibió derechos e: Brother of Amadeus IV, he received rights in Piedmont and ruled Flanders for his marriage to Joan. He was not the successor of his father in Savoy County.
Hermano de Arnaldo Roger II, recibió el: Brother of Arnaldo Roger II, he received the county of Pedro IV in 1343 and served the king in the campaigns of Rosellon (1343) and Mallorca (1349).
Hermano de Arnaldo Roger III, fue conde: Brother of Arnaldo Roger III, he was Count from 1369 to 1416 and married Blanca de Foix-Castellbó. He served Infante Juan and in the Panissars campaign of 1389–1390; after Caspe's engagement he supported Fernando de Antequera and participated in the pacification of the revolt of Jaime de Urgel (1412–1413).
Hermano de Carlos V y fundador de la ram: Brother of Charles V and founder of the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs. He reunited Austria, Bohemia and much of Hungary and eventually succeeded his brother in imperial dignity.
Hermano de David X, asumió la corona des: Brother of David X, he assumed the crown after his abdication and gave it to his nephew Luarsab. His brief government links two generations of the Bagrationi in a period of increasing Persian intervention.
Hermano de Enrique II, lo apartó del gob: Brother of Henry II, he removed him from the government of Cyprus and exercised the administration of the island. His marriage to Isabella of Armenia connected the Lusignans with the succession of sackcloth. He was murdered, which allowed Henry to return.
Hermano de Enrique III de Inglaterra, fu: Brother of Henry III of England, he was elected King of the Romans by a part of the electors. His candidacy competed with that of Alfonso X of Castile during the imperial interregno.
Hermano de Esteban Báthory, dirigió Tran: Brother of Stephen Bathory, he led Transylvania as a voivode while he reigned in Poland and retained princely dignity. His son Sigismund inherited a position marked by that overlapping of functions.
Hermano de Hetum II, obtuvo la corona tr: Brother of Hetum II, he obtained the crown after the assassinations of 1307. He tried to sustain the kingdom between the Mamluk threat and the search for Western support. Discussions on religious union accompanied his foreign policy.
Hermano de Hugh O’Neill y padre de Owen: Brother of Hugh O’Neill and father of Owen Roe, he links the generation of the Nine Years’ War with that of the Irish Confederation. His family maintained military and marriage connections between Ulster and the continent.
Hermano de Luis IX, participó en la cruz: Brother of Louis IX, he participated in the Egyptian crusade. He died in Mansura after an offensive that left the French forces in a very compromised situation.
Hermano de Luis XIII, participó en varia: Brother of Louis XIII, he participated in several conspiracies against Richelieu and real politics. His position as a possible heir gave him influence until the birth of the future Louis XIV.
Hermano de Luis XIV, fundó la rama moder: Brother of Louis XIV, he founded the modern branch of Orleans. He combined a subordinate position in court with a prominent military participation, especially in Cassel.
Hermano de Mauricio, elector de Sajonia: Brother of Mauritius, Elector of Saxony since 1553. He defended Orthodox Lutheranism, reorganized the administration of the electorate and gathered in Dresden a chamber of art and wonders.
Hermano de Miguel Antonio y Juan Ludovic: Brother of Miguel Antonio and Juan Ludovico, he agreed to the marquisate with French support after the succession crisis of 1528. His subsequent approach to the emperor changed that relationship.

Brother of Miguel Antonio and Juan Ludovico, he acceded to the marquis with French support after the succession crisis of 1528. His subsequent approach to the emperor changed that relationship. The succession passed to Gabriel, favored by France, while Juan Ludovico continued to defend his own rights. The conflict of the brothers weakened the autonomy of the marquisate.
Hermano de Otón Enrique, compartió desde: Brother of Otto Henry, he shared the Pfalz-Neuburg government since 1522. Between 1535 and 1541 both divided spheres of authority within the principality.
Hermano de Pedro I, gobernó durante la m: Brother of Peter I, he ruled during the minority of Peter II. The accusations and revenges that followed the assassination of the king confronted the members of the court. His title of prince of Antioch was nominal, as the principality had disappeared.
Hermano de Salomón I y padre de Salomón: Brother of Solomon I and father of Solomon II. His marriage to Helena, daughter of Heracli II, linked the last royal generation of Imereti with the united monarchy of Kartli-Kajetia.
Hermano de Vajtang VI, obtuvo el trono p: Brother of Vajtang VI, he obtained the throne first with Persian support and then under Ottoman domination. His changes of alliance and confession reflect the struggle for Kartli between the two powers and the factions of the royal family.
Hermano de Vlad III y rival por el trono: Brother of Vlad III and rival for the throne of Wallachia. With Ottoman support he replaced Vlad during the crisis of 1462 and embodies the complex policy of accommodation and resistance against Constantinople.
Hermano del cardenal Francesco Pignatell: Brother of Cardinal Francesco Pignatelli. He occupied viceroyalties in Sardinia and Sicily; a viceroy administered in the name of the monarchy and was not sovereign of those territories.
Hermano del papa León X, gobernó Florenc: Brother of Pope Leo X, he ruled Florence after the return of the Medici in 1512 and was Duke of Nemours. His tomb, the work of Michelangelo, is in the New Sacristy of St. Lawrence.
Hermano y sucesor de Luis V, gobernó el: Brother and successor of Louis V, he ruled the electoral Palatinate until 1556. Otto Henry, from the Neuburg branch, followed him.
