Hija de Alain de Albret y Françoise de C: Daughter of Alain de Albret and Françoise de Châtillon, she was sister to John III of Navarre. Her marriage to Cesare Borgia was part of the political connections between the French monarchy and the Italian world.
Hija de Alejandro VI y figura central de: Daughter of Alexander VI and central figure of the Borja dynastic alliances. After several political marriages she became Duchess of Ferrara and developed an important cultural court.
Hija de Alfonso IX de León y Berenguela: Daughter of Alfonso IX of León and Berenguela of Castile. He married John of Brienne, king of Jerusalem and later Latin emperor of Constantinople.
Hija de Amadeo IV, se casó primero con M: Daughter of Amadeus IV, she married Manfredo III of Saluzzo first and was the mother of Thomas I. After widowing she took part in the guardianship of her son and contracted a second marriage with Manfredo, future king of Sicily.
Hija de Amadeo V de Saboya y esposa de A: Daughter of Amadeus V of Savoy and wife of Andronicus III Paleologist. He was regent by his son John V during the civil war against John Cantacuceno (1341–1347).
Hija de Amadeo VII y Bona de Berry, se c: The daughter of Amadeus VII and Bona of Berry, she married John James of Monferrato. She was the mother of William VIII, Bonifacio III and Isabel, wife of Ludovico I of Saluzzo.
Hija de Arnaldo Roger I, fue condesa de: Daughter of Arnaldo Roger I, was Countess of Pallars from 1295 to 1330 against the claims of the Coserans, with the support of Jaime II. In 1297 he married Hugo de Mataplana, who ruled with her.
Hija de Bagrat III de Imericia, su matri: The daughter of Bagrat III of Imereti, her marriage to Luarsab I united the two western and eastern branches of the Bagrationi. She was the mother of Simon I and David XI, rivals who followed different policies in the face of safavid power.
Hija de Beka I de Samtsje y esposa de Al: Daughter of Beka I of Samtsje and wife of Alejo II of Trebizond. Andronico II's opposition to this marriage reveals that the family alliances of the Black Sea could contradict Constantinople's plans.
Daughter of Beka I and wife of Demetrius II. Through her, George V was linked to the house of Samtsje, whose support was important during his childhood and in the reconstruction of the royal authority.
Hija de Bernabò Visconti, se casó con Pe: The daughter of Bernabò Visconti, she married Peter II to strengthen relations between Milan and Cyprus. Her only daughter died a little. After widowing she returned to Italy; she should not be confused with Valentina Visconti, Duchess of Orleans.
Hija de Blanca I de Navarra y Juan de Ar: The daughter of Blanca I of Navarre and Juan de Aragón, she was the sister of Charles, Prince of Viana and Leonor. After the death of Carlos she was placed in the center of the dispute for Navarren rights in front of her father.
Hija de Bohemundo V y esposa de Enrique: Daughter of Bohemundo V and wife of Henry I of Cyprus, he exercised the regency of the island by his son Hugo II. His presence in Acre shows how Antioch's family alliances also influenced the politics of Jerusalem.
Hija de Carlos I de Albret, se casó con: The daughter of Charles I of Albret, she married John I of Foix and was the mother of Gaston IV. This marriage connected the Albret with the Foix-Grailly line before the later link of Catherine of Navarre and John III of Albret. Her presence reveals a family connection prior to the most well-known royal union.
Hija de Carlos II de Navarra, se casó pr: The daughter of Charles II of Navarre, she first married John IV of Brittany and was the mother of several members of the next ducal generation. Later she married Henry IV of England.
Hija de Carlos IV de Francia y Juana de: Daughter of Charles IV of France and Joan of Évreux, born a year before the death of her father. She died single in 1341.
Hija de Carlos IX y María del Palatinado: Daughter of Charles IX and Mary of the Palatinate. Her marriage to Juan Casimiro of the Palatinate-Zweibrücken connected the Vasa with a branch of Wittelsbach. Her son Carlos X Gustavo succeeded Cristina of Sweden: the dynastic name change did not break family continuity by female line.
Hija de Carlos de Orleans y María de Clé: The daughter of Charles of Orleans and Mary of Cléveris, she was the sister of Louis XII of France. Her marriage to Juan de Foix turned her sons Germana and Gaston of Nemours into nephews of the French monarch. This family relationship allows us to understand part of the international dimension of her trajectories.
Hija de Carlos de Valois y Catalina de C: The daughter of Charles of Valois and Catherine of Courtenay, inherited the title of Latin Empress of Constantinople, already without territory. Married to Philip of Tarento, she resided in the Angevin court of Naples.
Hija de Eduardo I y Leonor de Castilla,: Daughter of Edward I and Leonor of Castile, she married John II of Brabant. She was the mother of John III. Through her, the Brabantine ducal line was connected to England and Castile before her subsequent relationship with the Valois of Burgundy.
Hija de Enrique II de Champaña e Isabel: Daughter of Henry II of Champagne and Elizabeth of Jerusalem, he married Hugo I of Cyprus. He exercised regency functions and maintained rights and interests linked to both shores of the Mediterranean. His file connects the house of Champagne with Cyprus and Jerusalem, without reducing it to its later Navarre branch.
Hija de Enrique II y Leonor de Aquitania: Daughter of Henry II and Leonor of Aquitaine, he married William II of Sicily in 1177. Widow, accompanied his brother Richard in the third crusade and in 1196 married Raimundo VI of Tolosa. He died in 1199 and was buried in Fontevraud.
Hija de Enrique IV de Francia y María de: Daughter of Henry IV of France and Mary of Medici, he married Victor Amadeus I of Savoy. After widowing he defended the government of his sons against the princes of the ducal family, including Thomas Francis of Carignano.
Hija de Enrique IV de Inglaterra y María: Daughter of Henry IV of England and Mary of Bohun. Her marriage to Erik of Pomerania connected Lancaster monarchy with Kalmar.
Hija de Erik IV de Dinamarca y esposa de: Daughter of Erik IV of Denmark and wife of Magnus VI of Norway. She was mother of kings Erik II and Haakon V. After Magnus' death she participated in the government during the Erik minority, in a context of tensions between the crown, the aristocracy and the Church.
Hija de Federico Enrique de Orange y Ama: Daughter of Frederick Henry of Orange and Amalia of Solms. He married John George II of Anhalt-Dessau and exercised the regency for his son Leopold I between 1693 and 1698.
Hija de Felipe II e Isabel de Valois, se: The daughter of Philip II and Elizabeth of Valois, he married Charles Manuel I of Savoy. His marriage placed the descendants of the Duke within the family network of the Habsburgs and the Valois. Among his sons were Victor Amadeus I and Thomas Francis, for whom he continued the branch of Carignano.
Hija de Felipe III de España, esposa de: Daughter of Philip III of Spain, wife of Louis XIII and mother of Louis XIV. Regent of France since 1643 with Cardinal Mazarino, crossed the Fronda without losing power.
Hija de Felipe de Évreux y Juana II de N: Daughter of Philip of Évreux and Joan II of Navarre, she married Gastón Fébus. She was the mother of the count's legitimate son, also called Gastón.
Hija de Gastón IV de Foix y de Leonor de: Daughter of Gaston IV of Foix and Leonor of Navarre, she married Francis II of Brittany. She was the mother of Anne of Brittany. Her position allows her to travel through a direct connection between the Pyrenean houses and the Atlantic Duchy, without having to go through Ana's subsequent French marriages.
Hija de Gastón VII, aportó los derechos: The daughter of Gaston VII, she contributed the rights to Bearne to the offspring of her marriage to Roger Bernardo III of Foix. Her role is fundamental to understanding the origin of the patrimonial union.
Hija de Gian Galeazzo Sforza e Isabel de: Daughter of Gian Galeazzo Sforza and Isabel of Aragon, he married Sigismund I of Poland in 1518. He influenced the court of Krakow and in 1556 returned to his Duchy of Bari, where he died.
Hija de Guido de Dampierre, se casó con: The daughter of Guido de Dampierre, she married Floris V of Holland. She was the mother of John I, the last Dutch Count of that male line. Her marriage linked two neighboring houses whose heritage would end up meeting much later under the Dukes of Burgundy.
Hija de Guillermo IX y Ana de Alençon, s: Daughter of William IX and Anne of Alençon, her marriage to Frederick II Gonzaga was decisive for the transmission of Monferrato to that house. The inheritance required an imperial resolution and was not an automatic effect of weddings.
Hija de Guillermo Marshal e Isabel de Cl: Daughter of William Marshal and Elizabeth of Clare. Her marriage to Gilbert of Clare linked the family inheritance with the house that, through her daughter Elizabeth, would connect with the Bruce of Scotland.
Hija de Guillermo VIII de Monferrato, se: The daughter of William VIII of Monferrato, he married Charles I of Savoy. After the death of the Duke he assumed the regency for his son Carlos Juan Amadeo and defended his authority before the relatives of the house.
Hija de Guy de Bretaña y sobrina de Juan: The daughter of Guy of Brittany and niece of John III, he claimed the duchy in front of Juan de Montfort. Her husband, Carlos de Blois, defended his cause militarily.
Hija de Haakon V y Eufemia. Su matrimoni: Daughter of Haakon V and Eufemia. Her marriage to Erik Magnusson linked Norway with the Swedish house of Bjälbo. Her son Magnus inherited Norway and was elected king of Sweden in 1319. Ingeborg intervened in minority politics, although the councils of both kingdoms later limited his authority.
Hija de Heraclio II y esposa del príncip: Daughter of Heraclius II and wife of Prince Archil of Imereti. She was the mother of Solomon II: this connection helps explain the eastern support for her candidacy for the Western throne.
Hija de Hetum I y esposa de Bohemundo VI: Daughter of Hetum I and wife of Bohemundo VI. Her marriage reinforced the alliance between Armenia, Antioch and Tripoli; after the death of her husband she intervened in county politics during the Bohemundo VII minority.
Hija de Hugo III de Chipre y esposa de T: The daughter of Hugo III of Cyprus and wife of Theodore III of Armenia, she was the mother of Leo III. Her marriage is one of the direct links between the two monarchies, prior to the Lusignan's access to the sackcloth crown.
Hija de Jacobo II y reina de Inglaterra,: Daughter of James II and Queen of England, Scotland and Ireland along with William III. His accession to the throne consolidated the dynastic and political outcome of the Glorious Revolution.
Hija de James de Desmond, enlazó a los F: The daughter of James de Desmond, she linked the Fitzgeralds to the Butlers for their marriage to James de Ormond. After widowing she finally married Gerald de Desmond. Her family alliances went through political rivalry between the two houses.
Hija de Jorge X de Kartli y esposa de Te: The daughter of George X of Kartli and wife of Teimuraz I of Kajetia. The marriage strengthened the cooperation between the two branches during their wars against Persia. Their children linked this generation with the later kings of Kajetia and Imereti.
Hija de Juan II de Bretaña y Beatriz de: The daughter of John II of Brittany and Beatrice of England, she married Philip of Artois. Her offspring linked with the Évreux through Margaret of Artois. The Brittany-Artois-Évreux chain constitutes an important family connection between the Atlantic Duchy and the Navarrese monarchy.
Hija de Juan Jacobo de Monferrato y Juan: The daughter of John James of Monferrato and Joan of Savoy, he married Ludovico I of Saluzzo. His son Ludovico II thus gathered ancestry from the Saluzzo, the Italian Paleologists and the Savoy.

The daughter of Juan James of Monferrato and Joan of Savoy, she married Ludovico I of Saluzzo. Her son Ludovico II thus gathered ancestry from the Saluzzo, the Italian Paleologists and the Savoy. This family combination allows us to understand the Marquis’ ties with his neighbors, even if the kinship did not suppress rivalries over territories and inheritances.
Hija de Juan VI Cantacuceno y esposa de: Daughter of John VI Cantacuceno and wife of John V Paleologist, marriage that sealed peace after the Byzantine civil war of 1341–1347.
Hija de Juan de Borbón-La Marche y Catal: The daughter of John of Bourbon-La Marche and Catherine of Vendôme, she married Janus. She was the mother of John II and Anne of Cyprus. This union directly connects the Lusignans with the Bourbons and, by Anne, with the Savoy dynasty.
Hija de Juan de Foix y María de Orleans,: Daughter of Juan de Foix and Maria de Orleans, she was niece of Louis XII of France and second wife of Ferdinand the Catholic. Her position connected negotiations between France and Aragon with the Navarrese interests of her family.
Hija de Juan de Gante y Catalina de Roet: Daughter of Juan de Ghent and Catherine de Roet. By her marriage to Ralph Neville she was the mother of Cecily Neville and Ricardo de Salisbury: her offspring connected to the leading York leaders.
Hija de Juan sin Miedo y hermana de Feli: Daughter of John without Fear and sister of Philip the Good, she married Adolfo de Cléveris. She was the mother of Catherine, wife of Arnold of Egmond. That line connects the Dukes of Guelders with the Burgundian house that later intervened in his succession.
Hija de Leopoldo VI de Babenberg y de Te: Daughter of Leopold VI of Babenberg and Theodora, Constance of Austria married in 1234 Henry III, Margrave of Misnia. His marriage linked the Babenbergs to the Wettin. He was the mother of Albert and Dietrich; he died in 1243, before the Austrian succession crisis of 1246.
Hija de Levan de Kajetia y esposa de Sim: Daughter of Levan of Kajetia and wife of Simon I of Kartli. His family linked the two eastern monarchies through their children and grandchildren; these marriages coexisted with political rivalries and with the intervention of Persia and the Ottomans.
Hija de León II y Keran, se casó con Ama: The daughter of Leo II and Keran, she married Amalarch of Lusignan. After the death of her husband, her family was caught up in the struggles of the Armenian court. Her descendants inherited the claim that led the Lusignans to the sackcloth throne.
Hija de Lionel de Amberes y esposa de Ed: Daughter of Lionel de Antwerp and wife of Edmundo Mortimer, Count of March. His offspring linked an ancient branch of Edward III with Ana Mortimer and Ricardo of York.
Hija de Luis de Orleans y de Valentina V: Daughter of Louis of Orleans and Valentina Visconti, she married Richard of Brittany. Her son Francis II came to rule the duchy and was the father of Anne of Brittany. Through Margaret, that Breton heiress was connected to the families of Orleans and Milan before her own royal marriages.
Hija de Luis de Évreux y Margarita de Ar: Daughter of Louis de Évreux and Margaret of Artois, he married Charles IV of France. His marriage connected the branch of Évreux with the main line of the capeto kings.

Daughter of Louis de Évreux and Margaret of Artois, she married John III of Brabant. She was the mother of Joan of Brabant and Margaret, wife of Louis II of Flanders. Her offspring connect the Brabant and Flemish successions with the Capeta branch of Évreux.
Hija de Manfredo y esposa de Pedro III,: A daughter of Manfred and wife of Peter III, she preserved the dynastic connection between the Hohenstaufen and the new island monarchy. The Sicilian Vespers made that inheritance politically decisive. Her sons James and Frederick show that Aragon and Sicily could share a dynasty without retaining the same sovereign.
Hija de Manuel I de Portugal y de María: Daughter of Manuel I of Portugal and Maria of Aragon, he married his cousin Charles V in Seville in 1526. He ruled Castile during the emperor's absences and died in Toledo in 1539, after a difficult birth; he was the mother of Philip II.
Hija de Miguel VIII y hermana de Andróni: The daughter of Michael VIII and sister of Andronico II, his marriage to John II brought together the courts of Constantinople and Trebizond. He supported the Georgian marriage of his son Alejo II, linking the Palaiologists to the networks of the Caucasus.
Hija de Pedro I de Borbón e Isabel de Va: The daughter of Pedro I of Bourbon and Isabel of Valois, she married Arnaud-Amanieu of Albret. She was the mother of Charles I. Her filiation connects the Albrets with two capet branches and shows how a marriage alliance could add court relations to the territorial heritage of a house.
Hija de Petru Rareș y de su primera espo: The daughter of Petru Rareș and her first wife Maria, she married Mircea Ciobanul. After the death of her husband she led the policy of her son Petru’s government. The dismissal of 1568 led the family into exile. It still appears in news of 1587; it is not known here for a precise year for his death.
Hija de Reinaldo II, se casó con Guiller: The daughter of Reinald II, she married William of Jülich and transmitted rights to her children over Guelders. Her position explains the access of the house of Jülich after the death of her brothers. From her offspring also comes Arnold of Egmond's hereditary bond.
Hija de Roberto I de Artois, Blanca fue: Daughter of Robert I of Artois, Blanca was Queen Consort of Navarre for her marriage to Henry I. Al widower in 1274 defended the inheritance of her daughter Joan and negotiated her liaison with the future Philip IV of France. Her second marriage, with Edmundo de Lancaster, connected the house with the English monarchy.
Hija de Roger IV de Foix, se casó con Ja: Daughter of Roger IV of Foix, he married James II of Mallorca. That link connected the Pyrenean house with a monarchy whose heritage gathered island and continental spaces. Through its offspring you can follow the Mediterranean projection of the family of Foix.
Hija de Sancho VI de Navarra, se casó co: The daughter of Sancho VI of Navarre, she married Ricardo I in Limassol (Cyprus) in 1191, in the middle of a crusade. She never lived in England; after widowing she lived in Le Mans, which was part of her dowry, and there she founded the Abbey of L’Épau, where she is buried.
Hija de Sancho VI y hermana de Sancho VI: Daughter of Sancho VI and sister of Sancho VII, she married Teobaldo III of Champagne. After widowing she held the position of her son Teobaldo during her minority. For her, that son gathered a Navarrese hereditary right that became effective when his uncle Sancho VII died.
Hija de Teimuraz I, fue reina consorte d: Daughter of Teimuraz I, she was Queen Consort of Imereti and a decisive figure in her successor disputes. Following the death of Alexander III she intervened against Bagrat V and promoted Vajtang Tchutchunashvili. She died during another crisis of the Western court.
Hija de Teobaldo I de Navarra y Margarit: Daughter of Teobaldo I of Navarre and Margaret of Bourbon, she married Hugo IV of Burgundy. Her trajectory extended the connections of the house of Champagne beyond its French and Navarren heritage. She was one of the women by which the alliances of the family reached other ducal houses.
Hija de Teobaldo I de Navarra y de Inés: Daughter of Teobaldo I of Navarre and Agnes of Beaujeu, she married John I of Brittany. She was the mother of John II. Her position directly connects the Navarre dynasty of Champagne with the Breton dukes and helps to follow the relations between the two regions developed in this update.
Hija de Teodoro I de Monferrato, se casó: The daughter of Theodore I of Monferrato, she married Aimon of Savoy. Her ancestry was linked to Emperor Andronic II and to the Alleramic heiress Yolanda, named Irene in Byzantium.
Hija de Teodoro II de Morea y esposa de: Daughter of Theodore II of Morea and wife of John II, she favored the Greek institutions of Cyprus. She was the mother of Carlota. Her presence in the court allows to follow the links between the Lusignan Mediterranean and the last Byzantine world.
Hija de Tomás I de Saboya, se casó con R: Daughter of Tomás I of Savoy, he married Ramón Berenguer IV of Provence. His daughters linked with the French and English monarchies and the houses of Anjou and Cornwall.
Hija de Vajtang VI y esposa de Teimuraz: Daughter of Vajtang VI and wife of Teimuraz II, she linked the branches of Kartli and Kajetia. She was the mother of Heracli II, who would gather both crowns in 1762.
Hija de los Reyes Católicos, nacida en C: Daughter of the Catholic Monarchs, born in Córdoba in 1482, married in 1500 Manuel I of Portugal, widower of his sister Isabel. She was mother of John III of Portugal and Empress Isabel, and died in Lisbon in 1517.
Hija del almirante de Castilla Fadrique: Daughter of the Admiral of Castile Fadrique Enriquez and Marina de Córdoba, he married Juan II of Navarre and Aragon and was the mother of Fernando the Catholic. During the Catalan civil war he defended the rights of his son; he died in Tarragona in 1468.
Hija del duque Carlos I de Borbón, se ca: Daughter of Duke Charles I of Bourbon, she married Charles, Count of Charolais and future Duke of Burgundy in 1454. She died in 1465, before her husband inherited the duchy; her only daughter was Maria of Burgundy.
Hija del gran duque Francisco I de Tosca: Daughter of the Grand Duke Francis I of Tuscany and second wife of Henry IV of France. Regent for his son Louis XIII after the assassination of the king in 1610, she was banished after facing Richelieu.
Hija del rey Duarte de Portugal y de Leo: Daughter of King Duarte of Portugal and Leonor of Aragon, she married Frederick III and was crowned Empress in Rome in 1452. Mother of Maximilian I, died in 1467.
Hija del rey Jano de Chipre, se casó con: Daughter of King Janus of Cyprus, he married Louis of Savoy and brought to the Alpine court a direct connection with the Lusignans. His numerous offspring linked with France, Milan and the Cypriot succession itself.
Hija del señor serbio Constantino Dragaš: Daughter of Serbian lord Constantine Dragaš and wife of Manuel II Paleologist. She was the mother of the last two Byzantine emperors, John VIII and Constantine XI.
Hija póstuma de Carlos IV de Francia y d: Posthumous daughter of Charles IV of France and Joan of Évreux; her birth in 1328 confirmed the succession of Philip VI of Valois. In 1345 she married Philip, Duke of Orleans, son of Philip VI, and died in 1393 without descent.
Hija reconocida de Enrique IV de Castill: Renowned daughter of Henry IV of Castile and Juana of Portugal, she contested the Castilian succession to Isabel I. She was proclaimed queen by her supporters and married Alfonso V of Portugal in 1475. After the agreements of 1479 she lived in Portugal, where she died in 1530. The nickname "the Beltraneja" comes from an accusation about her fatherhood, not from a proven filiation.
Hijo de Adolfo I y María de Borgoña, suc: The son of Adolf I and Mary of Burgundy, succeeded in Cléveris in 1448. Mark’s trajectory was different; the county should not be confused with the entire Sauerland region.
Hijo de Alain de Albret y Françoise de C: The son of Alain de Albret and Françoise de Châtillon, he married Catherine of Navarre. Her royal position came from that marriage, while her birth home was Albret. The conquest of 1512 displaced the center of her monarchy and left her offspring a divided territorial and political heritage.
Hijo de Alejandro I y hermano de Vajtang: Son of Alexander I and brother of Vajtang IV, he participated in the distribution of power among the royal princes. His son Constantine II would retain Kartli when the monarchy was fragmented. His numbering and the scope of his authority varied between sources.
Hijo de Alejandro IV, ocupó brevemente u: Son of Alexander IV, briefly occupied a crown disputed by great lords and candidates Bagrationi. His murder opened another phase of intervention by the Gurieli and Abashidze in the government of Imereti.
Hijo de Alejandro VI, cardenal antes de: Son of Alexander VI, cardinal before becoming prince and commander. His rapid construction of a domain in Romagna was one of the most famous political examples studied by Machiavelli.
Son of Alejo II, he took power in 1332. His offspring allow him to continue the imperial genealogy until Alejo III, although this did not happen directly. The court went through several changes of ruler between the two generations.
Hijo de Alix de Thouars y Pedro de Dreux: Son of Alix de Thouars and Peter of Dreux, he inherited the duchy as a child. His father exercised government during his minority. John's marriage to Blanche of Champagne linked Brittany with the family reigning in Navarre; his son John II continued the ducal line.
Hijo de Amadeo VIII y María de Borgoña,: Son of Amadeus VIII and Maria of Burgundy, he assumed government functions before becoming Duke. His marriage to Anna of Lusignan linked Savoy to Cyprus.
Hijo de Andrónico II y de Irene de Monfe: Son of Andronico II and Irene of Monferrato, he passed from the Byzantine imperial family to the government of an Italian marquisate. His rights came from his mother, but he had to defend them against competitors.
Hijo de Andrónico II, asociado al trono: Son of Andronicus II, associated with the throne as co-emperor. He led campaigns against the Turks and the Catalan Company without success, and died before his father in 1320.
Hijo de Arnaud-Amanieu de Albret y Marga: Son of Arnaud-Amanieu of Albret and Margaret of Bourbon, he was lord of Albret and condestable of France. He died in the battle of Azincourt in 1415. His offspring connected the house both with the Foix, by his daughter Joan, and with the line that led to Alain and the Navarrese kings of Albret.
Hijo de Arturo II y de María de Limoges,: Son of Arthur II and Mary of Limoges, he was the brother of John III of Brittany and father of Joan of Penthièvre. He died before the Duke.
Hijo de Arturo II y de Yolanda de Dreux,: Son of Arthur II and Yolanda of Dreux, he contested the duchy to Joan of Penthièvre after the death of John III. His cause received English support and continued after his death, sustained by his wife and his son's supporters.
Hijo de Bagrat III, perteneció a la gene: The son of Bagrat III, belonged to the generation that disputed Western power to his relatives. His sons Rostom and George III successively occupied the throne, maintaining the genealogical continuity of the royal house.
Hijo de Bagrat V, regresó al trono con a: The son of Bagrat V, he returned to the throne with Ottoman support and faced the factions that favored Archil. His two reigns ended in further expulsions; his death did not end the rivalry between the two lines.
Hijo de Bagrat VII, heredó un poder estr: Son of Bagrat VII, he inherited a power closely dependent on Persia. The Georgian rebellion of 1625 displaced his authority and favored Teimuraz I. His death closed another safavid attempt to stabilize Kartli through this dynastic branch.
Hijo de Balduino II, último emperador la: Son of Baldwin II, last Latin emperor of Constantinople. After the Byzantine reconquest of 1261 he inherited only the title and married Beatrice, daughter of Charles of Anjou.
Hijo de Birger Jarl, elegido rey de Suec: Son of Birger Jarl, elected king of Sweden in 1250 under his father's regency. His brother Magnus deposed him in 1275.
Hijo de Bohemundo IV y esposo de Isabel: Son of Bohemundo IV and husband of Elizabeth of Cyprus. His son Hugo III inherited the Cypriot crown by the maternal line, retained the name Lusignan and brought to his descendants the genealogy of the princes of Antioch.
Hijo de Bonifacio III y hermano de Guill: Son of Boniface III and brother of William IX, he succeeded his nephew Boniface IV. He was the last Marquis of the legitimate male line of the Paleologists.
Hijo de Carlo Barberini y Costanza Magal: The son of Carlo Barberini and Costanza Magalotti, he was one of Urban VIII's cardinal nephews: his appointment, reserved since 1627, became public in 1628. He shared with his brothers Francesco and Taddeo the power and patronage of the family and, after 1644, the difficulties with Innocent X. He distinguished himself from his uncle, the Capuchin Cardinal of the same name.
Hijo de Carlos I y Blanca de Monferrato,: The son of Charles I and Blanche of Montferrat, Savoy inherited before his first birthday. His mother exercised the regency.
Hijo de Carlos II de Albret y padre de A: Son of Charles II of Albret and father of Alain, he died before his own father. Therefore he occupies an intermediate generation of genealogy without appearing as an equivalent link in the succession of lordship. The distinction helps to understand why a grandson could inherit directly from his grandfather.
Hijo de Carlos III, recibió en 1759 las: Son of Charles III, he received in 1759 the separate crowns of Naples and Sicily as a child. Revolutionary crises interrupted his control of the continent; both kingdoms formally joined in 1816.
Hijo de Carlos V y comandante de la Liga: Son of Charles V and commander of the Holy League in Lepanto. Philip II appointed him Governor General of the Netherlands in 1576. His recognition was partial and ended up facing the States; he died in 1578.
Hijo de Cathal Crobderg, defendió su pos: The son of Cathal Crobderg, he defended his position in Connacht by negotiating and fighting both with other Gaelic candidates and with the Anglo-Normans. His government shows the survival of a regional monarchy after the conquest begun in the 12th century.
Hijo de Conor y sobrino de Murrough, her: Conor’s son and Murrough’s nephew, he inherited the county within the agreement with the Tudor monarchy. Opposition from other members of the O’Brien shows the tension between the birthright of the English title and the rights of the Gaelic headship.
Hijo de Constantino I y padre de Bagrat: Son of Constantine I and father of Bagrat VI. His position in genealogy allows us to understand that the branch that ended up ruling Imereti came from the Georgian royal family itself, even though it faced other descendants of that house.
Hijo de Constantino II, fundó la rama pr: Son of Constantine II, he founded the princely branch of Mukhrani. His descendants reached the crown of Kartli with Vajtang V, so this line does not appear as a family isolated from the royal trunk.
Hijo de Cristian I y Dorotea. Reinó en D: Son of Cristian I and Dorotea. He reigned in Denmark and Norway before obtaining the Swedish crown in 1497.
Hijo de Daniel de Halych y yerno de Mind: The son of Daniel of Halych and son-in-law of Mindaugas, he received from Vaišelga the title of Grand Duke. His effective control appears to have been limited to the south and the Black Ruthenia. He was displaced by Traidenis; his death is dated in a dissenting manner in 1271 or 1279.
Hijo de Eduardo III de Inglaterra, recib: The son of Edward III of England, he received in 1385 the title of Duke of York and founded the house of York, one of the two branches faced in the Two Roses War.
Hijo de Eduardo III y hermano mayor de J: The son of Edward III and older brother of John of Ghent. His daughter Felipa transmitted to the Mortimers ancestry that Yorks invoked to claim the English crown.
Hijo de Enrique VIII y Juana Seymour, ll: The son of Henry VIII and Joan Seymour, he came to the throne as a child. During his brief reign the English Reformation advanced decisively under regency governments.
Hijo de Esteban Dušan y último emperador: Son of Stephen Dušan and last emperor of the Nemanjić dynasty. During his reign the great lords became independent and the Serbian Empire became fragmented.
Hijo de Esteban el Primer Coronado, rey: Son of Stephen the First Crowned, king of Serbia between 1228 and 1233. His brother Stephen Vladislaus removed him from the throne.
Hijo de Federico I. Su victoria en la gu: Son of Frederick I. His victory in the war of the Count consolidated the monarchy and made possible the implementation of the Lutheran Reformation. Norway’s reorganization reinforced its subordination to the Danish crown. The continuity of the common monarch thus lived with a profound change in institutions.
Hijo de Federico II de Sicilia y de Leon: The son of Frederick II of Sicily and Leonor of Anjou. In 1312 the Catalan Company, owner of Athens since the Battle of Cephisus, asked the king for a son as Duke, and Frederick named Manfredo, still a child. He never left Sicily: the duchy was ruled by vicars general. He died in Trapani in 1317 when he fell from the horse.
Hijo de Federico II de Sicilia y marqués: The son of Frederick II of Sicily and Marquis of Randazzo, he inherited in 1338 the ducats of Athens and Neopatria from his brother William. He ruled them, like his brothers, from Sicily through vicars, until his death in 1348.
Hijo de Federico II de Sicilia, heredó e: The son of Frederick II of Sicily, he inherited the Duchy of Athens in 1317 at the death of his brother Manfredo. Like him, he ruled from Sicily through vicars: his half-brother Alfonso Fadrique conquered the Southern Thessalia and formed in 1319 the Duchy of Neopatria, joined to that of Athens. He died in 1338.
Hijo de Federico II y rey de Sicilia, de: The son of Frederick II and king of Sicily, he defended the power of Hohenstaufen in Italy against the papacy. He died in Benevento fighting Charles of Anjou.
Hijo de Federico II, elegido rey de roma: Son of Frederick II, elected King of the Romans in 1220 and ruler in Germany on behalf of his father. He rebelled against him in 1234, was deposed and died in prison in 1242.
Hijo de Federico V e Isabel Estuardo, fu: The son of Frederick V and Elizabeth Estuardo, he was reinstated as elector for the Peace of Westphalia in 1648. He recovered a reduced Palatinate: Bavaria preserved the High Palatinate and the old electoral dignity.
Hijo de Felipe III de Francia, dio orige: Son of Philip III of France, he gave origin to the branch of Évreux. He married Margaret of Artois and was the father of Philip, future king of Navarre for his marriage to Joan II. His position explains the kinship of the new house without confusing him with the filiation proper to the Navarren queen.
Hijo de Felipe Luis y Ana de Jülich-Clév: The son of Philip Louis and Anna of Jülich-Cléneris-Berg, he obtained Jülich and Berg in the provisional division of Xanten in 1614. Clecheris, Mark and Ravensberg corresponded to Brandenburg.
Hijo de Felipe el Atrevido y Margarita d: Son of Philip the Atrevido and Margaret of Flanders, he inherited Brabant and Limburg in 1406. The connection came from the brabanon ancestry of his mother. He died in Azincourt; his sons John IV and Philip of Saint-Pol later ruled before the inheritance of Philip the Good.
Hijo de Fiódor Sanguszko y hermano de Ro: The son of Fyodor Sanguszko and brother of Román. His marriage to Halszka Ostrogska sparked a conflict over her guardianship and inheritance.
Hijo de Gastón Fébus e Inés de Navarra,: The son of Gastón Fébus and Inés of Navarra, he was called to continue the line of the county. He died in 1380, before his father, in the context of a violent family conflict. His absence in succession explains that, after the death of Fébus, he inherited a collateral branch of the Foix.
Hijo de Gastón I de Foix, representa la: Son of Gaston I of Foix, represents the family branch established in the Viscounty of Castellbó. This line retained its own position vis-à-vis the main one.
Hijo de Gastón IV de Foix y Leonor de Na: The son of Gaston IV of Foix and Leonor of Navarre, he married Magdalena of France. He was the father of Francis Phoebus and Catherine. He died before his mother came to the Navarren throne, so the succession passed to the generation of his children without him becoming king.
Hijo de Gastón IV y Leonor de Navarra, f: Son of Gaston IV and Leonor of Navarre, he was the brother of Gaston, Prince of Viana, and uncle of Catherine of Navarre. He married Maria of Orleans. His sons Germana and Gaston of Nemours link this branch to the Aragonese court and to the French campaigns in Italy.
Hijo de Grace O’Malley y Richard Bourke,: The son of Grace O’Malley and Richard Bourke, he maintained family influence through agreements with the Crown. He received the Viscount of May in the 17th century. His career shows the transformation of Gaelic chiefdoms into titled nobility.
Hijo de Guillermo I de Henao, fue tambié: The son of William I of Henao, was also William IV of Holland. He died in a campaign in Friesland without leaving any legitimate offspring. Her sister Margaret and her children placed the inheritance of the three counties in the orbit of the Wittelsbach.
Hijo de Guillermo IX y Ana de Alençon, h: The son of William IX and Anne of Alençon, Monferrato inherited at the age of six, under guardianship. He died young and without offspring, so his uncle Juan Jorge succeeded him.
Hijo de Guillermo Ramón, vizconde de Bea: The son of Guillermo Ramón, Viscount of Bearne since 1224. He accompanied Jaime I in the conquest of Mallorca and died in the battle of Portopi on 12 September 1229, together with Ramón de Moncada. His son Gastón VII succeeded him.
Hijo de Guillermo de Orange y Luisa de C: Son of William of Orange and Louise de Coligny, Frederick Henry succeeded his half-brother Maurice in 1625 as Prince of Orange and stadtholder of several provinces. He distinguished himself in siege warfare, notably at ’s-Hertogenbosch and Maastricht. His marriage to Amalia of Solms strengthened the court and the house’s alliances.
Hijo de Guillermo de Orange, Mauricio di: Son of William of Orange, Maurice commanded the armies of the United Provinces and served as stadtholder of several provinces. His campaigns consolidated the revolt against the Spanish monarchy. He inherited the principality of Orange in 1618 and clashed politically with Johan van Oldenbarnevelt, who was executed in 1619. Maurice died in 1625.
Hijo de Guillermo el León. Reinó de 1214: Son of William the Lion. He reigned from 1214 to 1249 and consolidated the Anglo-Scotish border before dying during a campaign in the west.
Hijo de Gustavo Vasa y Margarita Leijonh: The son of Gustavo Vasa and Margaret Leijonhufvud. As Duke and leader of the opposition to his nephew Segismund, he pushed the power shift that removed the Polish branch from the Swedish throne. He was the father of Gustavo II Adolfo and Catherine, whose offspring led to Carlos X Gustavo.
Hijo de Gustavo Vasa, rey de Suecia desd: The son of Gustavo Vasa, king of Sweden since 1560. He began Swedish expansion in Estonia (Reval, 1561) and the Seven Years Nordic War against Denmark. After the murders of the Sture (1567) and his marriage to Karin Månsdotter, his brothers deposed him in 1568; he died in prison in 1577.
Hijo de Hetum I e Isabel, sufrió cautive: Son of Hetum I and Elizabeth, he suffered captivity after the Mamluk invasion of 1266. As king he continued to seek Mongolian support in front of Egypt. His numerous offspring linked Armenia with Byzantium and the Lusignan.
Hijo de Hugo III y hermano de Enrique II: The son of Hugo III and brother of Henry II, he held the post of condestable. He did not manage to reign, but his son Hugo IV inherited the crown after Henry's death. His marriage linked him to the Ibelin of Beirut.
Hijo de Hugo III, rey de Chipre y titula: Son of Hugo III, king of Cyprus and titular of Jerusalem since 1284. He died in 1285 after a year of reign and succeeded him by his brother Henry II.
Hijo de Hugo de Mataplana y de la condes: Son of Hugo de Mataplana and Countess Sibila, he shared the county with his mother until 1330 and ruled until 1343. He died without children, and Pedro IV granted Pallars to his brother Ramón Roger.
Hijo de Isabel de Foix-Castellbó y Archa: The son of Isabella de Foix-Castellbó and Archambaud of Grailly, he continued the heritage of Foix under a new male descent. His marriage to Juana de Albret connected both houses before the navarra royal union of the end of the 15th century. His son Gastón IV married Leonor of Navarre.
Hijo de Jaime Fadrique y conde de Salona: Son of James Fadrique and Count of Salona since 1365. His cousin Frederick III of Sicily named him in 1375 vicar general of the ducats; upon the death of the king he avoided anarchy, and in 1380, by the chapters of Athens, Peter IV of Aragon confirmed him by uniting the ducats to the Crown. He died in 1382.
Hijo de Jorge IV y primo de David Narin,: Son of George IV and cousin of David Narin, he received Mongolian confirmation to share the throne. His government was linked to Iljanato's campaigns and fiscal demands; after the western separation he retained the eastern nucleus.
Hijo de Juan I de Cléveris y padre de Ju: Son of John I of Cléveris and father of John III. He ruled Cléveris and Mark before the marriage of his heir to Mary of Jülich-Berg gathered both dynastic lines.
Hijo de Juan I y Blanca de Champaña, se: The son of John I and Blanca of Champagne, he married Beatrice of England. With him come the Breton ducal heritage, the navarra connection of his mother and the English connection of his wife. His son Arthur II was the father of the lines between which the duchy would later be disputed.
Hijo de Juan II e Isabel de Mallorca, he: Son of John II and Isabella of Mallorca, Monferrato inherited after his brother John III. His government was crossed by relations with Milan and by disputes with Savoy-Acaya.
Hijo de Juan II y de Beatriz de Inglater: The son of John II and Beatrice of England, he succeeded in the duchy in 1305. He had offspring from his marriages with Mary of Limoges and Yolanda of Dreux.
Hijo de Juan IV de Bretaña y de Juana de: The son of John IV of Brittany and Joan of Navarre, he belonged to a smaller branch of the Montfort. He married Margaret of Orleans, linking the Breton house with the Valois-Orleans.
Hijo de Juan IV y Juana de Navarra, gobe: Son of John IV and Joan of Navarre, he ruled Brittany during a decisive phase of the Hundred Years' War. His marriage to Joan of France reinforced the connection with the Valois. He appears as John V or John VI according to the ducal numbering adopted; the two names correspond to the same person.
Hijo de Juan Jacobo y Juana de Saboya, c: The son of Juan Jacobo and Juana de Savoy combined the government of Monferrato with the military service of the Italian powers. His daughters married Ludovico II of Saluzzo and Charles I of Savoy.
Hijo de Juan Jacobo, sucedió a su herman: The son of Juan Jacobo, succeeded his brother William VIII when expectations of Monferrato’s inheritance already affected Savoy and Saluzzo. His sons William IX and John George extended the male line of the Paleologists.
Hijo de Juan V o VI de Bretaña y de Juan: Son of John V or VI of Brittany and Joan of France, he inherited the duchy in 1442. His government belongs to the final phase of the Hundred Years' War, when relations between the French and English powers changed. Upon his death, the succession passed to his brother Peter II.
Hijo de Juan de Foix y María de Orleans,: The son of John of Foix and Mary of Orleans, he was nephew of Louis XII and brother of Germana of Foix. He led French forces during the wars of Italy and died in the Battle of Ravenna in 1512. His career brings together the Pyrenean connections of the Foix and military service to the French monarchy.
Hijo de Juan de Gante y Catalina de Roet: The son of John of Ghent and Catherine of Roet, he was legitimized along with his brothers in 1397 and received the county of Somerset. He was the father of Duke John Beaufort and grandfather of Margaret Beaufort, mother of Henry VII.
Hijo de Juan de Randazzo, heredó en 1348: Son of John of Randazzo, he inherited in 1348 the ducats of Athens and Neopatria. He died in 1355, and the ducats passed to their cousin King Frederick III of Sicily.
Hijo de Lazar Hrebeljanović y déspota de: Son of Lazar Hrebeljanović and despot of Serbia. He sailed between Ottoman pressure and Hungarian influence while turning Belgrade into an important political and cultural center.
Hijo de Ludovico II y Margarita de Foix-: The son of Ludovico II and Margarita de Foix-Candale, defended a favorable orientation for Charles V. His mother and his brothers removed him from power on several occasions.

Son of Ludovico II and Margaret of Foix-Candale, he inherited Saluzzo as a child. He developed his career in the service of the French monarchy, while his mother retained a decisive role in the marquisate.
Hijo de Luis VI de Francia, recibió el c: The son of Louis VI of France, he received the county of Dreux and gave rise to a branch of the Capeta family. His estate offered his descendants a position of its own within the French nobility.
Hijo de Luis de Saboya y Ana de Chipre,: The son of Louis of Savoy and Anna of Cyprus, he married his cousin Carlota. His royal dignity came from that marriage and was then reduced to a pretense in exile. It should not be confused with his father, Duke of Savoy.
Hijo de Luis y Ana de Chipre, llegó al d: The son of Louis and Anna of Cyprus, he came to the duchy by extinguishing the male offspring of his brother Amadeus IX. His brief government preceded those of his sons Filiberto II and Charles III, born of different marriages.
Hijo de Magnus Eriksson y Blanca de Namu: Son of Magnus Eriksson and Blanca de Namur. He ruled Norway and briefly shared Swedish royalty with his father. He married Margaret, daughter of Valdemar IV of Denmark. His son Olaf inherited Norway when he was already Danish king: the marriage prepared a union whose access occurred on different dates.
Hijo de Magnus III y hermano del rey Bir: The son of Magnus III and brother of King Birger. His rivalry with Birger was part of a family crisis that ended with his captivity and death. His marriage to Ingeborg of Norway was decisive: his son Magnus gathered in 1319 the Norwegian heritage and the Swedish election.
Hijo de Magnus VI y de Ingeborg de Dinam: The son of Magnus VI and Ingeborg of Denmark. His marriage to Margaret of Scotland made him the father of the so-called Norwegian Maiden, a Scottish heiress who died before settling in the kingdom. Erik died without a surviving male son and his brother Haakon V succeeded him.
Hijo de Mamuka, fue instalado con apoyo: Mamuka's son, was installed with Ottoman support in front of his cousin Solomon I. His defeat allowed the restoration of this. The episode shows that the divisions of the royal house facilitated the outside intervention.
Hijo de Manuel Filiberto, gobernó en un: The son of Manuel Filiberto, he ruled in a scenario dominated by rivalries between France and the Spanish Monarchy. His marriage to Catherine Micaela connected him to Philip II.
Hijo de Manuel II, gobernó el despotado: The son of Manuel II, he ruled the despotate of Morea in a stage of Byzantine expansion in the Peloponnese. His daughter Helena became queen of Cyprus, linking the last Palaeologists with the Lusignans.
The son of Marjorie Bruce and Walter Stewart. In 1371 he became the first king of Stewart's House.
Hijo de María de Bearne y de Guillermo d: Son of Mary of Béarn and William of Montcada, he was Viscount of Béarn and, through his marriage to Petronilla in 1196, Count of Bigorre. In 1213 he paid homage to Peter II of Aragon and fought beside him against the French crusaders. He died without issue and was succeeded by his brother William Raymond.
The son of Maria de Bearne and Guillermo de Moncada, he succeeded his brother Gastón VI as Viscount of Bearne in 1215. He died in 1224 and was followed by his son Guillermo.
Hijo de María de Borgoña y Maximiliano d: The son of Mary of Burgundy and Maximilian of Habsburg, he inherited the Netherlands and, after Senlis (1493), the Franche-Comté and Artois. He preserved the dignity of Duke of Burgundy, although the duchy was under the French Crown. His marriage to Juana I took him to Castile and transmitted heritages other than Charles V.
Hijo de Mircea Ciobanul y Chiajna, acced: The son of Mircea Ciobanul and Chiajna, he accepted the principality at the age of twelve. His mother maintained a decisive intervention in the government.

The son of Mircea Ciobanul and Chiajna, he agreed to the principality at the age of twelve. His mother maintained a decisive intervention in the government. Ottoman authority deposed him in 1568 and died that same year in exile. His trajectory allows us to distinguish the young holder from the one who led much of the politics.
Hijo de Radu el Grande, gobernó Valaquia: Son of Radu the Great, he ruled Wallachia in three stages separated by displacements and restorations. He married Chiajna, daughter of Petru Rareș of Moldova.
Hijo de Raimundo VI y de Juana de Inglat: The son of Raimundo VI and Joan of England, he married in 1211 to Sancho of Aragon. He led his father the reconquest of Toulouse in front of the Montfort and succeeded him in 1222; by the Paris Treaty of 1229 he accepted that the county pass to his daughter Juana, married to Alphonse of Poitiers. He died in Millau in 1249.
Hijo de Ramón Berenguer IV y Petronila,: Son of Ramón Berenguer IV and Petronila, first king who inherited the kingdom of Aragon and the county of Barcelona, since 1164. He extended his influence to Provence and the south of France.
Hijo de Ramón Roger II, gobernó de 1350: Son of Ramón Roger II, he ruled from 1350 to 1366 and fought in the Two Peters war against Pedro I of Castile.
Hijo de Ricardo de Bretaña, accedió al d: The son of Richard of Brittany, he agreed to the duchy after the lines of his relatives who had preceded him were extinguished. He tried to maintain the Breton political autonomy against the French monarchy.
Hijo de Roberto I Bruce, rey de Escocia: Son of Robert I Bruce, king of Scotland since 1329. He spent years exiled in France and eleven captives in England after being defeated at Neville's Cross (1346).
Hijo de Roger Bernardo I, gobernó de 142: The son of Roger Bernardo I, he ruled from 1424 to 1451. He was convicted of Aragon and in 1438 rejected a French invasion of the Arán valley; he dragged debts and lawsuits with Queen Mary, with John of Foix and with the Bellera.
Hijo de Roger Bernardo III y de Margarit: The son of Roger Bernardo III and Margaret of Béarn, he continued the joint heritage of Foix and Bearne. His sons originated different paths within the family: the Gaston II line and that of Roger Bernardo de Castellbó.
Hijo de Roger I, fue conde de Pallars So: Son of Roger I, he was Count of Pallars Sobirà from 1234 to 1256. He married Sibila of Berga.
Hijo de Roger II, gobernó Pallars de 125: Son of Roger II, he ruled Pallars from 1256 to 1288. He was tutor to Count Ermengol X of Urgel and rebelled against the Crown in 1275 and 1280; then he served Peter III in the expedition to Tunis in 1282 and in the defense of Ampurdan in 1285.
Hijo de Rusudán, compartió la corona con: Son of Rusudan, he shared the crown with his cousin David VII by Mongol decision. After rebelling, he consolidated his power in the west: the monarchy of Imereti was born from a fracture of the kingdom, not a new dynasty.
Hijo de Sibila de Jerusalén, coronado ni: Son of Sibilah of Jerusalem, crowned a child with his uncle Baldwin IV. He died in 1186 at barely nine years old, opening up the succession crisis that preceded the fall of Jerusalem.
Hijo de Stefan y Angelina, compartió ini: A son of Stefan and Angelina, he initially shared the dignity of despot with his brother Đorđe. The title was exercised in the Hungarian sphere and did not mean that Serbia had been recovered. His daughter Jelena married Petru Rareș, linking the Branković descendants with the Moldavian court.
Hijo de Stefan y Angelina, conservó el t: Son of Stefan and Angelina, he retained the title of Serbian despot in exile. He abandoned secular life and took the name Maximus. His religious activity and relationship with Krušedol continued the family presence in the region. It should not be confused with the homonymous historian of the seventeenth century.
Hijo de Sten Sture el Joven y Cristina G: Son of Sten Sture the Younger and Cristina Gyllenstierna. He developed his career under the monarchy of the Vasa and received a countal rank. He was one of the victims of the Sture massacres ordered by Erik XIV in 1567, an episode that aggravated the crisis of the reign.
Hijo de Svante Nilsson y regente de Suec: Son of Svante Nilsson and regent of Sweden. He faced Cristian II and the pro-union party. He died after being wounded in the campaign of 1520; his wife Cristina Gyllenstierna then led the resistance in Stockholm. The defeat gave way to the brief Swedish royalty of Cristian.
Hijo de Teodoro I, continuó en Monferrat: Son of Theodore I, continued in Monferrato the branch of the Paleologists arrived from Byzantium. His marriage to Isabella of Majorca added a connection to the Majorcan royal house.
Hijo de Teodoro II, heredó Monferrato y: Son of Theodore II, Monferrato inherited and married Joan of Savoy, sister of Amadeus VIII. The kinship did not prevent the pressure of the saboyan duke on his domains.
Hijo de Teodoro III, accedió al trono ba: Son of Theodore III, he acceded to the throne under the tutelage of his uncle Hetum II. Both were killed by Mongolian chief Bilarghu. The crisis showed that the alliance with the Mongols did not guarantee the security of the Armenian monarchy.
Hijo de Tomás Francisco de Saboya-Carign: Son of Thomas Francis of Savoy-Carignano, he inherited from his mother the county of Soissons and served as a general in the armies of Louis XIV. He married Olympia Mancini, niece of Mazarino, and was the father of Prince Eugene.
Hijo de Tomás Francisco y María de Borbó: The son of Thomas Francis and Mary of Bourbon-Soissons, continued the branch of Carignano. Her marriage to Angela Caterina of East added an Italian connection to the Savoyard and Bourbon heritage.
Hijo de Tomás II, accedió al condado tra: Son of Thomas II, he entered the county after the death of his uncle Philip I. His position was consolidated by agreements with other branches of the family, which retained their own rights. Edward and Aimon succeeded in Savoy; by their marriages, the count also linked with Bâgé and Brabant.
Son of Vajtang V and father of Vajtang VI. He carried out responsibilities in the Georgian government and in the Safavid court. His sons were candidates for the throne at a time when Persian investiture and local control did not always coincide.
Hijo de Vajtang V, fue instalado en dife: Son of Vajtang V, he was installed at different times in Kajetia and Imereti. His repeated losses of the throne led him to Russian exile, where he developed his literary activity. He unites the three territorial branches without turning them into a single permanent crown.
Hijo de Vlad II Dracul, accedió brevemen: The son of Vlad II Dracul, briefly came to power in 1481 and recovered him the following year. His continuity until 1495 opens a family path different from that of his brother Vlad III. His son Radu the Great extended this Basarab line in the Wallachia government.
Hijo de Walter Butler y padre del futuro: Son of Walter Butler and father of the future Duke of Ormond. He died in a shipwreck before inheriting the county, so the succession passed directly from his father to his son James.
Hijo del condestable Carlos I, continuó: The son of Countess Charles I, he continued the house of Albret after the death of his father in Azincourt. The line passed by his son John of Tartas led to Alain de Albret. His position allows to reconstruct the stately continuity between the 15th century and the generation linked to Navarre.
Hijo del emperador Fernando I, archiduqu: Son of Emperor Ferdinand I, Archduke of Austria Interior since 1564. His son Ferdinand II brought this branch of Styria to the imperial throne.
Hijo del estatúder Guillermo V, fue proc: Son of Stadtholder William V, he was proclaimed the first King of the Netherlands in 1815, when the kingdom also included Belgium, and became Grand Duke of Luxembourg. The Belgian Revolution of 1830 separated the south; he abdicated in 1840.
Hijo del rey Alberto I de Habsburgo. En: Son of King Albert I of Habsburg. In 1306 he was elected king of Bohemia after the extinction of the Premislids, but died in campaign the following year.
Hijo del rey Juan Balliol, reclamó el tr: Son of King John Balliol, he claimed the Scottish throne with English support in front of David II. He was crowned in 1332, but he never consolidated his authority and resigned in 1356.
Hijo extramatrimonial de Juan II, obtuvo: The son of John II, who was born out of wedlock, obtained Mamluk help to dispute the crown to Carlota and recovered Famagusta from the Genoese. Her marriage to Catherine Cornaro reinforced the Venetian influence. She died before the birth of her heir.
Hijo mayor de Felipe V, reinó apenas uno: Philip V's eldest son, he reigned only a few months in 1724 after his father's abdication. He died of smallpox at the age of seventeen and Philip V returned to the throne.
Hijo mayor del emperador Fernando III, c: The eldest son of Emperor Ferdinand III, crowned king of Bohemia and Hungary and elected King of the Romans in 1653. He died of smallpox in 1654 without succeeding his father.
Hijo mayor superviviente de Enrique II,: Henry II's surviving eldest son, was crowned king in life of his father in 1170, but he never received effective power. He led the great rebellion of 1173–1174 with his brothers and the support of France, and died in 1183, before his father.
Hijo menor de Amadeo V, heredó después d: Amadeus V's youngest son, inherited after his brother Edward, whose daughter also defended inheritance rights. His marriage to Yolanda de Monferrato united the Savoy with the new Italian branch of the Paleologists.
Hijo menor de Carlos Manuel I y Catalina: A younger son of Charles Emmanuel I and Catherine Michelle, he began the branch of Savoy-Carignano. He married Marie de Bourbon-Soissons and participated in the disputes against the regency of Christine of France.

The youngest son of Charles Emmanuel I and Catherine Michelle, began the Savoy-Carignano branch. He married Marie de Bourbon-Soissons and participated in the disputes against the regency of Christine of France. His military career alternated alliances in a context of European war; his offspring would arrive much later on to the Sardinian throne with Carlos Alberto.
Hijo menor de Cristian I y tío de Cristi: A younger son of Cristian I and uncle of Cristian II. He was elected king after the deposition of his nephew in 1523, while Gustavo Vasa consolidated the Swedish break.
Hijo menor de Felipe VI de Francia y Jua: The youngest son of Philip VI of France and Joan of Burgundy, he received in 1344 the Duchy of Orleans. He fought in Poitiers (1356) and was held hostage in England after the treaty of Brétigny; he died in 1375 without legitimate children.
Hijo menor del duque de Lorena, fue nomb: The youngest son of the Duke of Lorraine, he was appointed first Duke of Guisa in 1528 and founded one of the great noble houses of France. His daughter Mary of Guisa was Queen of Scotland and mother of Mary Stuart.
Hijo natural de Federico II de Sicilia,: The natural son of Frederick II of Sicily, he ruled since 1317 the Catalan ducats as vicar general of his half-brother William. He conquered Siderocastro and the Southern Thessaly, with which he formed in 1319 the Duchy of Neopatria. He married in 1317 Marulla of Verona and founded the branch of the Fadrique, Counts of Salona and lords of Egina.
Hijo natural del rey de Sicilia, gobernó: A natural son of the king of Sicily, he ruled the duchy on behalf of his half-brother William.
Hijo o hija de su predecesor: Son or daughter of his predecessor
Hijo póstumo de Godofredo de Bretaña, fu: The posthumous son of Godofredo of Brittany, he was a candidate for the Angevin inheritance in front of his uncle Juan Sin Tierra with the support of Felipe Augusto. Captured in Mirebeau in 1202, he disappeared in 1203; his death, attributed to John, precipitated the loss of Normandy.
Hijo y sucesor de Luis VI, fue padre de: The son and successor of Louis VI, he was the father of Philip II and brother of Robert I of Dreux. His position links the main line of the Capetian kings with the comital branch.

The son and successor of Louis VI, he was the father of Philip II and brother of Robert I of Dreux. His position links the main line of the Capetian kings with the comital branch. The transmission of the crown to Philip II continued on a different path than that which would lead the descendants of Robert to the Duchy of Brittany.
Hijo y sucesor de Raimundo Roger, fue co: Son and successor of Raimundo Roger, he was Count of Foix from 1223 to 1241. His marriage to Ermesenda (1208) united the Viscounts of Castellbó and Cerdaña to the house. His protection of the Albigenses and his rejection of the Inquisition earned him new excommunications.

Jefe de los O’Neill que aceptó el título: Chief of the O’Neill who accepted the title of Earl of Tyrone in 1542. The agreement with Henry VIII did not eliminate Gaelic succession or family disputes: both systems legitimized different candidates.

Primer duque catalán, nombrado niño a pe: First Catalan duke, named child at the request of the Company. He did not leave Sicily: they ruled vicars general.
Primer duque de Cléveris, se casó con Ma: First Duke of Cléveris, married Mary of Burgundy. Her daughter Catherine brought that connection to the duchy of Guelders through her marriage to Arnold of Egmond. The alliance placed her grandchildren within the family network of the Valois of Burgundy.
Primer duque de Florencia (1532), impues: First Duke of Florence (1532), imposed with the support of Charles V, whose natural daughter Margaret married him. He was murdered in 1537 by his cousin Lorenzino de Medici.
Primer duque de Milán de la casa Viscont: First Duke of Milan of the Visconti house. Through war, diplomacy and territorial purchases he built a domain that aspired to become the great power of northern Italy.
Primer emperador de la casa de Luxemburg: First emperor of the house of Luxembourg. He tried to restore imperial authority in Italy, but his early death left incomplete a project that anticipated the rise of his dynasty.
Primer gobernante ruso coronado como zar: First Russian ruler crowned as Tsar. He expanded the state towards Volga and Siberia, but his reign was also marked by the violence of oprichnina and serious internal crises.
Primer landgrave de Hesse-Darmstadt. La: First Landgrave of Hesse-Darmstadt. The division of Hesse became his own political actor, later closely linked to the houses of Brunswick and Hanover.
Primer landgrave de Hesse-Kassel tras la: First Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel after the partition of the heritage of Philip I. His branch became one of the most durable and active princely houses in the center of Germany.
Primer rey Borbón de España. La Guerra d: First Bourbon king of Spain. The War of Succession made him lose Milan, Naples and Sardinia; he recovered the latter briefly between 1717 and 1720. His peninsular and Italian domains followed different paths.
Primer rey Borbón de Francia y antiguo r: First Bourbon king of France and former king of Navarre. He ended much of the French religious wars and rebuilt monarchic authority after decades of conflict.
Primer rey coronado de la dinastía Neman: First crowned king of the Nemanjić dynasty. His reign consolidated the political independence of Serbia and opened the monarchic stage that would culminate with the empire of Stefan Dušan.
Primer rey de la casa de Trastámara en C: First king of the house of Trastámara in Castile. He reached the throne after a civil war against Peter I and founded a new dynasty destined to dominate much of the Iberian politics of the 15th century.
Primera esposa de Antonio de Borgoña, fu: First wife of Antonio de Burgundy, she was the mother of John IV de Brabant and Philip de Saint-Pol. Her two sons successively occupied the ducats of Brabant and Limburg. The absence of offspring of both opened the inheritance to their cousin Philip the Good.
Primera reina de Inglaterra que gobernó: First Queen of England who ruled in her own right effectively. Daughter of Henry VIII and Catherine of Aragon, she tried to restore Catholicism and was married to Philip II of Spain.
Primera reina reinante de Portugal. Su g: Portugal’s first reigning queen. Her government reversed some of the Pombal policies, but her mental deterioration eventually transferred effective power to her son Juan.
Princesa Médici convertida en reina y re: Princess Medici became queen and regent of France. She tried to maintain the balance of the monarchy during the wars of religion and the confrontation between Catholic and Protestant factions.
Princesa de Carignano de la dinastía Bor: Princess of Carignano of the Bourbon-Condé dynasty. Her trajectory is linked to France, Savoy.
Princesa de Carignano de la dinastía Est: Princess of Carignano of the East Dynasty. Her trajectory is linked to Modena, Savoy.
Princesa de Carignano de la dinastía Hes: Princess of Carignano of the Hesse dynasty. Her trajectory is linked to Hesse, Savoy.

Princesa de Carignano de la dinastía Sab: Princess of Carignano of the Savoy dynasty. Her trajectory is linked to Savoy.
Princesa de Carignano de la dinastía Wet: Princess of Carignan of the Wettin Dynasty. Her trajectory is linked to Saxony, Savoy.
Princesa de Orange de la dinastía Estuar: Princess of Orange of the Estuardo Dynasty. Her trajectory is linked to England, the Netherlands.
Princesa de Orange de la dinastía Hohenz: Princess of Orange of the Hohenzollern dynasty. Her trajectory is linked to Prussia, the Netherlands.

Princesa de la casa de Gonzaga-Nevers, f: Princess of the house of Gonzaga-Nevers, was queen of Poland as the successor wife of Ladislaus IV and his brother John II Casimiro, over whose politics he had great influence.
Princesa de la dinastía Aldobrandini. Su: Princess of the Aldobrandini dynasty. Her trajectory is linked to Rome.

Princesa de la dinastía Lusignan. Su tra: Princess of the Lusignan dynasty. Her trajectory is linked to Cyprus, Jerusalem.
Princesa georgiana, tomó el nombre de Eu: Georgian princess, took the name Eudoxia and married Manuel III. She was the mother of Alejo IV. Her file connects two Black Sea courts without attributing a territorial government to her for her status as consort.
Principado con instituciones y gobierno: Principality with its own institutions and government under Ottoman sovereignty; it is distinguished from real Hungary and the provinces directly administered by the Sultan.
Principado de Pfalz-Neuburg creado tras: Pfalz-Neuburg Principality created after the Landshut succession war (1505). It is not equivalent to the electoral Palatinate; the map represents the nuclei of Neuburg and Burglengenfeld with their partitions and imperial occupation.
Procedente de Mukhrani, fue adoptado com: From Mukhrani, he was adopted as heir by Rostom and recognized by the Sah. He extended the influence of his family towards Kajetia and Imereti through his children. His trajectory combines Bagrationi legitimacy with the safavid investiture.

Proclamó la independencia de Brasil y se: He proclaimed the independence of Brazil and became its first emperor. Later he intervened in the Portuguese civil war in defense of the rights of his daughter Mary II.
Promovió expediciones contra los poderes: He promoted expeditions against the Muslim powers of the Eastern Mediterranean and sought support in the European courts. Recibió la corona kajetia en el contexto: He received the kajetia crown in the context of the safavid collapse and briefly occupied Tbilisi in front of Vajtang VI. Ottoman intervention altered his alliances and ended with his death. His brother Teimuraz later reorganized the eastern power.
Recibió la corona mientras continuaba al: He received the crown while continuing to serve the safavids outside Georgia. He died during the Kandahar campaign. Vajtang, his brother, administered Kartli, so his title is not represented as a continuous face-to-face government.

Reclamación durante la ocupación frances: Claim during the French occupation; restitution in 1493.
Reconocido por Conn Bacach como hijo y h: Recognized by Conn Bacach as the county’s son and heir, he was rejected by Shane O’Neill and murdered by his supporters. His fatherhood was discussed: the recognized bond is preserved, pointing to that uncertainty.
Reconocido por Persia, permaneció allí h: Recognized by Persia, he remained there until 1719.
Reconquista de 1717; evacuación y transf: Reconquest of 1717; evacuation and transfer to Savoy in 1720.
Recuperó Constantinopla en 1261 y fundó: He regained Constantinople in 1261 and founded the last Byzantine imperial dynasty. He combined diplomacy and military intervention to contain Charles of Anjou; the marriages of his sons linked his house with the powers of the Black Sea.
Recuperó brevemente los dominios de su p: He briefly recovered his father's domains.
Recuperó el ducado de Lorena en 1697 por: He recovered the duchy of Lorraine in 1697 for the peace of Ryswick and ruled it until 1729. He was the father of Francis Stephen, husband of Mary Theresa and emperor.
Recuperó el trono en varias ocasiones me: He regained the throne on several occasions through changing alliances and Ottoman support. The interventions of the Gurieli and other nobles interrupted his authority. His sons Alexander V and George IX extended the royal branch during the 18th century.
Recuperó la corona navarra después de ha: He regained the Navarren crown after having been excluded from the French succession. His reign with Philip of Évreux again separated the political trajectories of Navarre and France.
Redujo los recursos militares del Imperi: He reduced the military resources of the Byzantine Empire in a context of serious fiscal difficulties. The arrival of the Catalan Company and the war with his grandson Andronic III aggravated the crisis.
Reforzó la administración y la legislaci: He strengthened the administration and legislation of Poland and promoted the foundation of the University of Krakow. He was the last Polish king of the main line of the Piast.
Reforzó la autoridad castellana tras una: He strengthened Castilian authority after a conflictive minority. During his reign the stately conquest of the Canary Islands began and diplomatic contacts developed with the court of Tamerlan.
Reforzó la autoridad real y reunió terri: He strengthened royal authority and gathered fragmented territories during Mongol rule. He maintained relations with Italian merchants and with the powers of the Eastern Mediterranean.
Reforzó la corte y la marina escocesas y: He strengthened the Scottish court and navy and maintained the alliance with France. He died in Flodden, a defeat left by another royal minority in Scotland.
Regencia del cargo hereditario de Guille: Regency of the hereditary office of William V during his minority; provincial authority of the States, not sovereign monarchy over the Republic.
Regencia para sus hijos Federico y Maria: Regency for his sons Federico and Mariano; the sources call it giudicessa, but the judicial succession corresponds to the children. The end of 1404 is conventional and discussed.
Regente de Anhalt-Zerbst, 1747–1752 (reg: Regent of Anhalt-Zerbst, 1747–1752 (Regency), Princess of the Holstein-Gottorp dynasty.

Regente sueco después de Sten Sture el V: Swedish regent after Sten Sture the Elder. His government continued to resist the authority of King John. Reina de Castilla y una de las figuras c: Queen of Castile and one of the central figures of the formation of the Hispanic Monarchy. He ruled alongside Fernando de Aragón and presided over a decisive stage of political and territorial expansion.
Reina de Escocia desde la infancia y rei: Queen of Scotland since childhood and Queen Consort of France for her marriage to Francis II. Her life was marked by religious struggles, the Scottish nobility crisis and her dynastic rivalry with Elizabeth I.
Reina de Inglaterra durante una etapa de: Queen of England during a period of political consolidation, maritime expansion and religious conflict. Her long reign was associated with the Elizabethan cultural boom and rivalry with Spain.
Reina de Jerusalén desde 1131, hija de B: Queen of Jerusalem since 1131, daughter of Baldwin II. She ruled with Fulco and then with her son Balduino III, until he took power in 1152. She was a great religious promoter.
Reina de Jerusalén desde 1186, hermana d: Queen of Jerusalem since 1186, sister of Baldwin IV. She crowned her husband Guido of Lusignan, under whose reign Jerusalem was lost to Saladin in 1187.
Reina de Jerusalén desde 1190, hija de A: Queen of Jerusalem since 1190, daughter of Amalaric I. Her successive husbands, Conrad of Montferrato, Henry of Champagne and Amalarch of Lusignan, ruled the kingdom with her.
Reina de Jerusalén desde 1205, hija de I: Queen of Jerusalem since 1205, daughter of Elizabeth I and Conrad of Montferrato. She married John of Brienne and died shortly after giving birth to Elizabeth II.
Reina de Jerusalén desde su nacimiento e: Queen of Jerusalem since her birth in 1212, daughter of John of Brienne and Mary of Montferrato. Married in 1225 to Emperor Frederick II, she died when she gave birth to Conrad in 1228.
Reina de Mallorca, 1375–1406 (pretensión: Queen of Majorca, 1375–1406 (pretension). Pretentious of the Casa de Aragón dynasty.
Reina de Polonia por derecho propio y es: Queen of Poland in her own right and wife of Ladislao Jagellon. Her marriage linked Poland to Lithuania and had decisive consequences for Christianization and Eastern European politics.
Reina de Suecia, hija de Gustavo II Adol: Queen of Sweden, daughter of Gustavo II Adolfo, famous for his intellectual and cultural interest. He abdicated in 1654, converted to Catholicism and spent much of his life in Rome.
